papers.title: Entanglement distillation, nonlocal magic, and state sharing in an isospectral non-Hermitian bipartite model
papers.abstract: An invertible nonunitary similarity deformation leaves a two-qubit Hamiltonian's spectrum unchanged while varying a selected normalized right eigenstate in the fixed physical inner product. We embed this state in a two-parameter maximally correlated family that includes local dephasing and noisy circuit preparation. Hashing and a matching diagonal relative-entropy bound give the exact distillable entanglement and the PPT comparison distances at every finite tensor power. Correlated PPT catalysts cannot improve the Bell-pair distillation rate. The optimized CHSH value is \(2\sqrt{1+t^2}\): every state with nonzero coherence violates CHSH, while complete dephasing is separable. A calibrated finite-sample bound and two equal-fidelity preparations clarify which noise parameters determine the rate. For pure inputs, the binomial Schmidt spectrum gives logarithmic collectively optimized nonlocal magic with vanishing density, despite a positive entanglement density and extensive pairwise-frame magic. Fixed Clifford decoding gives six- and eight-copy CCZ concentration probabilities \(P_6=\frac12(1-2^{-\mathcal M_γ})\) and \(P_8=1-2^{-\mathcal M_γ}\). The same family permits explicit swapping recursions, symmetry-resolved entanglement, and a comparison of qubit stabilizer and fermionic Gaussian resources. These calculations keep the relevant operation classes separate when comparing many-copy limits.

papers.title: Unified quantification of entanglement and nonstabilizerness in information scrambling and their trade-off relation
papers.abstract: Entanglement and nonstabilizerness are among the most fundamental properties unique to quantum systems. Each quantity captures a different aspect of non-classical behavior, and each can be regarded as a resource within its own operational setting. However, the interrelation between them has not yet …

papers.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement as a probe of many-body localization in disordered spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions
papers.abstract: We study the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) in a disordered system and its potential for detecting the transition from the thermalized to the localized phase. We demonstrate that the quenched average GME can approach its near-maximum value in the ergodic phase of a disordered quantum spin m…

papers.title: TCBP-JOBS: GPU-Accelerated Quantum Error Correction Decoding and Noise Learning with Near-Optimal Accuracy
papers.abstract: Achieving near-optimal quantum error correction (QEC) decoding accuracy often requires computationally expensive searches that limit both large-scale simulation and real-time operation. We introduce trajectory-calibrated belief propagation (TCBP), which learns calibrated fault probabilities from BP trajectories, and jittered OSD beam search (JOBS), which uses these probabilities to guide parallel GPU searches. Across surface, color and bivariate-bicycle code memory and surgery circuits, TCBP-JOBS achieves logical error rates comparable to those of the Tesseract most-likely-error decoder at physical error rates of 0.1% to 0.4%, and up to 4.5$\times$ lower on the largest codes. Serial speedups over Tesseract's sparsified presets range from 10$\times$ to 7,400$\times$, and against unsparsified long-beam Tesseract they reach 13,000$\times$ on the bivariate-bicycle codes, at logical error rate ratios of 0.97 to 1.57. At lower physical error rates ($10^{-4}$ to $5\times10^{-4}$), rare-event splitting on the gross code shows that Tesseract is more accurate. Batched execution accelerates offline simulation for rapid, efficient exploration of large-scale QEC design spaces. For QPUs with longer logical clock cycles, our serial memory and logical-surgery experiments demonstrate accuracy comparable to Tesseract while meeting the millisecond-scale latency requirements of online feed-forward operation. Beyond memory and logic decoding, we demonstrate using TCBP-JOBS for confidence scores for postselection in memory and magic-state cultivation, enabling end-to-end color code cultivation. Together, these methods provide a GPU framework for accelerating QEC research via accurate decoding, noise estimation, and confidence assessment.

papers.title: A Forward Bit Makes Error Correction Dispensable for Antidegradable Amplitude-Damping Channels
papers.abstract: Preserving a qubit usually relies on redundant encoding over many uses of a noisy channel. We prove that for antidegradable amplitude damping, one channel use with one forward classical bit matches or beats every forward-assisted or unassisted code with any number of uses. We then show that variational circuits learn to switch from error correction to classical assistance as damping grows, beating a dual-certified bound on all unassisted three-use codes and, relative to the best unassisted see-saw, extending storage time by up to 13% at entanglement fidelity down to 0.65.

papers.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
papers.abstract: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cramér-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.

papers.title: Entanglement and information dynamics in charged dual-unitary circuits with impurities
papers.abstract: Local parts of a closed, non-equilibrium quantum many-body system can reach stationarity through the buildup of entanglement between different regions. In this paper we investigate how this process is affected by the presence of a quantum impurity that breaks a global symmetry of the bulk. In particular, we study a charged dual-unitary quantum circuit perturbed by a symmetry-breaking, non-dual-unitary gate acting on a spatially fixed pair of sites. In this setup we calculate the entanglement entropy for a subsystem that does not contain the impurity, as well as the mutual information and logarithmic negativity for a bipartite subsystem that straddles the impurity. We obtain exact results in the early time regime for these quantities from the dual unitarity of the bulk system. Beyond this regime, we compute the predictions of the quasiparticle and entanglement membrane pictures, supporting them with exact calculations obtained by taking the corresponding limits of the bulk entangling power. We find that the presence of a symmetry-breaking impurity can lead to a richer behaviour of quantum relaxation, including non-monotonic evolution of the entanglement entropy, a modification of the long-time steady state, and persistent subsystem mutual information and entanglement negativity. This behaviour is understood in terms of long-range correlations generated by scattering from the impurity, and facilitated by the ballistic propagation of the conserved charges.

papers.title: Observing Enhanced Entanglement in an Ising Quantum Register Beyond Weak Measurement
papers.abstract: Measurements often yield a disentangled quantum state which is the most probable measurement outcome while the measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement could be exponentially less probable or absent. Higher probability in measurement outcomes with enhanced entanglement is virtue in experimental observation of enhance entanglement in post-selected or Born-rule measurements with less resources in noisy quantum devices. We develop a periodic measurement sampling(PMS) protocol in the framework of uniform matrix product states. Using PMS, we identify a peak enhancement of entanglement in a uniform post-measurement state whose probabilistic outcome can be maximized by optimizing a measurement super-cell. A measurement super-cell is the smallest repeating building block of qubits defined by the measurement density, external field strength and exchange interactions between quantum register and ancilla qubits. The above prediction based on a classical description of the many-body quantum state is demonstrated in a quantum computing experiment in a loop of quantum register qubits with Ising interactions in the presence of transverse magnetic field. Further, we show the scalability of predictions of the periodic measurement sampling protocol in the thermodynamic limit to finite size systems. Especially, we present a rescaling ansatz which would enable predicting the possibility of observing enhanced entanglement in finite size systems.

papers.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
papers.abstract: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

papers.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
papers.abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

papers.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.

papers.title: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Continuous quantum error correction promises reduced thresholds and hardware overhead compared to the digital paradigm, but its complex model estimation has greatly reduced its practicality. We recast this problem as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy made of an exact bilinear reduced model, an exact conditional filter, and standard estimation and feedback design. For any $[[n,k,d]]$ stabilizer code whose generators are all continuously monitored and which is driven by a single Pauli recovery channel, we prove that the exact filter closes at dimension $3\cdot2^{\,n-k-1}$. This dimension is set by the syndrome space instead of the Hilbert space and is minimal within invariant-subspace filtering. The reduced model exposes and corrects two failure mechanisms of the feedback loop. Strong monitoring damps the rotational partner through which the controller steers the stabilizer and injects back-action diffusion along the recovery path; lowering the measurement strength during correction raises the entanglement fidelity of partner-steering LQR control by $0.096$ in the three-qubit code with three monitored parities. Linearizing at the codespace leaves the syndrome uncontrollable, so the controller can stall; a gain designed at a shifted operating point removes this degeneracy. In the limit of zero measurement during correction, we prove that a syndrome-only filter is exact at every recovery boundary. The resulting committed-recovery controller needs only $2^{\,n-k}$ class probabilities and gives the highest entanglement fidelity compared among the methods tested in the literature, $0.947$ against $0.920$ for a measurement-based estimator protocol in the three-qubit bit-flip code, and $0.726$ vs at most $0.407$ for continuous controllers in the five-qubit perfect code.

papers.title: Holographic representation of one-dimensional many-body quantum states via isometric tensor networks
papers.abstract: Tensor network methods, most prominently matrix product states (MPS), have become fundamental tools in modern quantum many-body physics. While MPS and extensions like the multiscale entanglement renormalization ansatz (MERA) and tree tensor networks (TTN) efficiently capture area-law entanglement an…

papers.abstract: Quantifying multipartite entanglement in quantum many-body systems and hybrid quantum computing architectures is a fundamental yet challenging task. In recent years, thermodynamic quantities such as the maximum extractable work from an isolated system (the ergotropy) have allowed for entanglement me…

papers.title: Circuit-Level Analysis of Quantum Error Correction in Second-Generation Quantum Repeaters
papers.abstract: We present a circuit-level simulation of second-generation quantum repeaters with stabilizer-based quantum error correction. We model a two-segment repeater link including encoding, syndrome extraction, decoding, and entanglement swapping, and compare the performance of the single-error-correcting Steane and five-qubit stabilizer codes under different noise scenarios. To that extent, we consider noise sources with incoherent (depolarizing and dephasing) and coherent (systematic over-rotation) errors and incorporate them directly at the circuit level. While the Steane code outperforms the five-qubit code at coherent errors, the five-qubit code achieves higher end-to-end fidelities under incoherent noise in the low-noise regime when a large number of physical qubits is affected by it. At higher noise regimes, employing no code turns out to be the best option. In mixed noise scenarios, we observe moderate cross-effects between the noise classes regarding the error correction performance. We conclude that code selection in second-generation quantum repeaters must be adapted to the dominant physical noise mechanism and that circuit complexity and hardware-aware implementation options influence performance in coherent-error-dominated regimes, providing design insights for error correction in quantum repeaters.

papers.title: Entanglement, correlations, and resource costs for symmetry-adapted quantum simulations of light through medium-mass nuclei
papers.abstract: Entanglement governs both the classical cost of simulating correlated many-body systems and the quantum resources needed to treat them. In this work, we use nuclear symmetries to investigate the entanglement and correlations in nuclei using \textit{ab initio} symmetry-adapted no-core shell-model nuclear wavefunctions, illustrated here for $^{4,6,8}$He, $^8$Be, $^{12}\mathrm{C}$, $^{20}\mathrm{Ne}$, and $^{48}$Ca. In this many-body approach, deformation and collectivity naturally emerge from the underlying chiral potential, and we show that the Sp(3,$\mathbb{R}$) basis concentrates the ground state in far fewer basis states than the SU(3) basis. We compute single-mode entropies and two-mode mutual information, and examine the organization of like-particle two-nucleon correlations into symmetry channels. Single-mode entropies are largest in the valence shells, while two-mode mutual information reveals substantial correlations both within and between shells. In all cases considered, the dominant pair correlations are captured by fewer SU(3) channels than angular-momentum channels, which reduces the number of variational parameters. Since the number of operator components within the channels is comparable in the two schemes for the heavier nuclei, this gives the SU(3)-coupling scheme a clear advantage. Fiedler ordering of the correlation graph with local refinement reduces the register ordering cost by a factor of 2 to 3 relative to the original shell ordering, and by 10 when two more shells are included in the register. Together, these measures link nuclear correlations to the selection of active modes and candidate excitation operators and to the design of quantum register layouts, offering guidance for the development of hybrid quantum-classical calculations of nuclei.

papers.title: Page Curve for Local-Operator Entanglement from Free Probability
papers.abstract: The local-operator entanglement (LOE) measures the classical simulability of a Heisenberg operator and is conjectured to witness many-body chaos in locally interacting systems. Using tools from free probability, we analytically compute its asymptotic value for Haar random dynamics for all Rényi indi…

papers.title: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases. By extending the stability experiment for many cycles, we uncover a sum-of-exponentials behavior in error suppression caused by a temporally correlated error: data-qubit heating to the third excited state $|3\rangle$. We fully capture this effect with a parameter-free, device-level leakage model incorporating higher-state transport during syndrome extraction cycles. To suppress this error, we develop and realize a walking stability circuit, reaching a logical error probability floor of $\le 3.20\times 10^{-8}$ at 60 cycles---two orders of magnitude below the standard construction---and limited by ionizing radiation error bursts. Finally, by adaptively terminating syndrome extraction based on decoder confidence in an offline analysis, we reduce spacetime logical error by 38% and time overhead by 34% compared to the optimal fixed-cycle strategy.

papers.title: The speed limit of gravitational entanglement and the cost of noise
papers.abstract: Is gravity quantum? A proposed test lets two small masses, each in a superposition of two places, become entangled through their mutual gravity. Gravity is weak, so the masses must stay coherent for seconds while random forces disturb them. Here we ask how fast gravity can entangle two masses, and what noise costs. Without noise we find the maximum rate exactly: it falls as the inverse cube of the separation, and two positions per mass achieve it. Above a noise level set by the masses and their separation, gravity's leading pull can be imitated by classical signals, and every strategy is limited to a rate falling at least as the inverse fourth power. Exact, continuous error correction shields the masses from noise but hides them from each other: the best rate falls as the inverse seventh power, and six positions on a hexagon come within 10% of it at large separation.

papers.title: Catalytic compression of classical communication in exact entanglement transformations
papers.abstract: Entanglement catalysis is usually associated with making otherwise impossible transformations possible. Here we show that it can also change how much classical communication a transformation requires. A catalyst, returned exactly and uncorrelated with the output, can reduce the message alphabet size required for exact transformations of bipartite pure states by a factor that grows without bound as the Schmidt rank increases. In the asymptotic many-copy regime, however, this advantage disappears at the level of the leading communication rate: the optimal catalytic and noncatalytic rates coincide. We characterize the optimal catalytic cost in terms of Rényi entropies, revealing how the entanglement structure of the source and target governs the finite-copy advantage. Our results establish reusable entanglement as a resource for compressing classical communication in quantum state manipulation.

papers.title: Stabilizer-Restricted Antidistinguishability in Quantum Computation with Magic States
papers.abstract: An antidistinguishing measurement for a family of preparations excludes at least one preparation for every possible outcome, constraining 'classical' representations of these processes, known as ontological models. We develop this connection within quantum computing with magic states (QCM), a universal model of quantum computation. Our constructions use adaptive Pauli measurements on tensor products of single-qubit non stabilizer states, including families associated with the Clifford hierarchy. These constructions yield stabilizer-restricted versions of the Pusey-Barrett-Rudolph theorem: any ontological model reproducing these measurement statistics and satisfying preparation independence must assign disjoint ontic supports to the preparations considered. We demonstrate this obstruction to preparation independence in a concrete ontological model based on convex polytopes used for the classical simulation of QCM.

papers.title: Ultraviolet structure of entanglement harvesting from energy density and other quadratic couplings
papers.abstract: We study entanglement harvesting with particle detectors coupled to the renormalized energy density of a massless scalar field. Our analysis identifies the distributional mechanism underlying the persistent ultraviolet divergences previously observed for quadratic detector couplings and shows that t…

papers.title: Activating entanglement and Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen steering from continuous-variable resources using witness-based measures
papers.abstract: The authors show that it is possible to faithfully measure any quantum resource via entanglement. They also provide a way to convert any resource into an equivalent amount of entanglement.

papers.title: Squeezed superradiant lasing of a quantum many-body emitter
papers.abstract: In conventional lasers, the emitters are typically incoherent, radiating photons independently; in superradiant lasers, many coherent emitters radiate photons cooperatively, but they essentially do not interact with each other. Here, we present the concept of quantum many-body lasers, in which the e…

papers.title: Genuine multipartite entanglement in ring-shaped Hubbard models
papers.abstract: Spin states can be extracted from many-electron systems by detecting electrons at a set of lattice sites, which act as particle labels. Here we quantify the genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) of such spin states, which are generally mixed, in standard and extended Hubbard rings, together with the corresponding detection probability. We show that the on-site repulsion, by suppressing charge fluctuations, enhances the GME, and that in the strongly interacting regime at half filling the detection probability decreases only weakly with the number of spins. The GME is robust at temperatures below the singlet--triplet gap, and can even be enhanced by doping, in spite of the induced charge fluctuations. The transition from spin- to charge-density waves in the extended Hubbard model is signaled by an abrupt suppression of both the GME and the detection probability.

papers.title: Unruh-induced decoherence and entanglement degradation in Ramsey interferometry
papers.abstract: We propose a modified Ramsey interferometric protocol to probe decoherence associated with the Unruh effect through fringe visibility. The scheme employs Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum through an interaction that induces pure dephasing without transitions between their internal energy levels. For a uniformly accelerated detector with finite spatial extent, an analytical dephasing function separates inertial vacuum fluctuations from the thermal Unruh contribution. When the thermal contribution dominates, fringe visibility decays exponentially with a rate proportional to the proper acceleration. The bipartite extension considers two detectors initially prepared in a Bell state, one inertial and the other uniformly accelerated, while retaining correlations mediated by the scalar field. In particular, we find that the joint fringe visibility coincides exactly with concurrence when the cross-term contribution disappears. This suggests that the entanglement degradation can be quantified directly from the interference contrast.

papers.title: Coherence, Entanglement and Complementarity in Mixed Classical Light
papers.abstract: The classical analogues of quantum correlations have been the subject of considerable interest in the past few years; however, all of these investigations consider the classical analogue of pure quantum mechanical states only. In this work, we study mixed classical light states and derive relations between the polarization coherence of the field and the (classical) entanglement between its degrees of freedom. We show, for a specific model of mixed states, where the purity is determined by a single parameter, how the coherence shared between polarization and entanglement shrinks as the level of purity decreases. The sum of the square of polarization and entanglement remains constant, a behaviour consistent with previous results [Phys. Rev. Lett. 117, 153901 (2016)] of pure states, even though the constant for the mixed state case is now smaller in value.

papers.title: Study of Randomness in Quantum Random Number Generator using Bayesian Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We propose a Bayesian neural network (BNN) framework to quantify the intrinsic (aleatoric) uncertainty in a continuous-variable quantum random number generator (CV-QRNG). This provides a direct data-driven measure of the QRNG's randomness generation. The BNN is trained on raw homodyne voltage time-series data from a fiber-coupled vacuum-fluctuation QRNG (VFQRNG). For each voltage data segment, the network predicts a Gaussian distribution (mean and variance) for the next sample, and the ensemble-averaged predicted variance is used as a diagnostic of entropy-related behavior under assumptions of our quantum source model. Thus, the predicted variance serves as a BNN model-based monitor of the randomness-generation process. We validate that the BNN metric increases with the local-oscillator (LO) power, consistent with theoretical min-entropy (extractable randomness). We also show the metric is sensitive to practical imperfections, coarse-graining (simulating limited analog-to-digital converter (ADC) sampling) or reducing ADC bit depth causes a clear drop in predicted aleatoric uncertainty, consistent with the source min-entropic model. These results establish the BNN-based metric as a complementary, physically motivated diagnostic tool for QRNG characterization. Unlike conventional tests (e.g. autocorrelation) that miss hardware issues like low ADC resolution, our method provides a direct real-time monitor of the VFRNG performance. Therefore, this metric is useful for real-time monitoring of CV-QRNG conditions, including drifts and other imperfections.

papers.title: Holographic Entanglement after a Global Quench in Noncommutative Yang-Mills Theory
papers.abstract: The time evolution of holographic entanglement entropy and mixed-state correlations following a global quench in four-dimensional N=4 noncommutative Yang-Mills theory is investigated using a Vaidya geometry. For strip-shaped regions extended along a noncommutative direction, two distinct early-time growth regimes emerge, depending on the relation between the shell-crossing and noncommutative scales: logarithmic growth, with a coefficient proportional to the injected energy density and the square of the noncommutative scale, followed by quadratic growth. For sufficiently wide strips, an intermediate linear-growth regime appears, governed by an entanglement velocity that increases with noncommutativity. The approach to equilibrium is also examined, revealing the role of the butterfly velocity in the continuous evolution of extremal surfaces, while competing branches can modify the physical saturation time. For two disjoint strips, the leading width-independent logarithmic contribution cancels in the mutual information, whereas the entanglement wedge cross section exhibits an intermediate linear-growth regime governed by the same entanglement velocity, provided the connected entanglement wedge remains dominant.

papers.title: Fragmentation in Non-Hermitian Many-Body Systems
papers.abstract: In non-Hermitian (NH) fermionic chains with spatially random imaginary gauge fields, single-particle eigenstates exhibit erratic NH skin localization with strongly fluctuating, subexponential decay, distinct from both conventional skin accumulation and Anderson localization. At finite filling, Pauli exclusion suppresses macroscopic accumulation and instead leads to fragmentation of the particle density, in sharp contrast to Hermitian disordered systems. Using exact free-fermion methods, we show that the density organizes into disconnected regions of high and low occupancy, forming spatially separated Fermi domains whose number $N_{\mathrm{FS}}$ scales subextensively with system size $L$. Remarkably, fragmentation is not only an equilibrium property but also emerges dynamically in the NH evolution, unlike in Hermitian systems where such structures are not dynamically selected. This behavior admits a Coulomb-gas description in a stochastic potential, establishing a direct link between erratic NH skin localization and real-space fragmentation of many-body states.

papers.title: Dissipation as a Resource for Entanglement via High-Spin Mediator Purification
papers.abstract: We study entanglement generation between two spin qubits mediated by a single, thermally mixed, high-spin ($S=5/2$) magnetic impurity, using the Lindblad master equation to compare coherent and dissipative control of the mediator. We show that no coherent drive, however strong or resonant, can purify the mediator beyond its thermal value --- a direct consequence of unitary evolution exactly preserving state purity --- while a dissipative channel purifies it up to the limit set by the optical pumping cycle itself, $\mathrm{Tr}[ρ_M^2]\approx0.8$. Modeling this channel with rates fixed by the measured optical pumping of a single Mn spin, we find that the entanglement it enables is not monotonic in the pump strength: it peaks at a finite rate and then decreases, since the same channel leaks decoherence to the qubits through the coupling that mediates their entanglement. At the experimental pumping rate, a single $80$ns pulse purifies the mediator, the resulting polarization persists for a timescale three orders of magnitude longer than the entangling dynamics, and the first-recurrence negativity rises from $0.18$ to $0.64$ at $12$K, remaining above $0.6$ up to $30$K. These results establish dissipation, not as noise to be suppressed, but as the very resource that makes robust entanglement generation possible.

papers.title: Temporal Complexity Hierarchies in Solvable Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Researchers establish a framework based on geometric group theory to classify the temporal computational complexity and quantum memory structures of solvable quantum many-body dynamics.

papers.abstract: We study a random theory of semiclassical guiding center motion for a many-electron system in a strong magnetic field. papers.abstract: We develop a unified many-body theory of two-photon dark-state laser cooling, the workhorse for preparing trapped ions close to their motional quantum ground state. For ions with a Λ level structure, driven by Raman lasers, we identify an ion-number-dependent crossover between weak and strong coupli…

papers.abstract: Scalable generation of multipartite entanglement in noisy quantum devices is a key challenge for quantum technologies. Drawing inspiration from the established experimental ability in entanglement generation of photonic memristors, we introduce an unsupervised optimization framework that realizes a …

papers.title: Mixed-state entanglement and phase transitions in Einstein-Born-Infeld massive gravity
papers.abstract: We study mixed-state entanglement measures in Einstein-Born-Infeld massive gravity theory, a model exhibiting both Hawking-Page phase transitions and effective metal-insulator transitions (MIT) at finite temperatures. Our comprehensive investigation reveals that the entanglement wedge cross-section …

papers.title: Benchmarking superconducting quantum processors with percolating entanglement quality
papers.abstract: The capability to create large entanglement resources is a key performance attribute of quantum processors, and the size of the resource is often used as a benchmark of processor scale. Recent graph-state experiments have reported entanglement clusters spanning entire chips with hundreds of qubits. However, cluster size alone does not capture the entanglement quality of individual couplings or differences in coupling topology. Here, we introduce percolating entanglement quality (PEQ), a topology-normalized benchmark based on conditional two-qubit negativity and a topology-specific bond-percolation threshold. As an experimental demonstration, we prepare a native graph state on a 64-qubit square-lattice superconducting processor with defects, identify a 52-qubit entanglement cluster, and evaluate the PEQ of the processor. Applying PEQ to previously reported chip-wide graph-state measurements on heavy-hex-lattice processors, we show that PEQ differs substantially among processors whose entanglement clusters span the entire chip. PEQ provides a single chip-wide score without selecting a best-performing qubit subset or path. This score allows processors with different coupling topologies to be compared on a common scale and can inform the design of coupling topologies for scalable chips.

papers.title: No universal LOCC entanglement purification
papers.abstract: Entanglement purification aims to obtain high-fidelity entangled states from noisy entangled states. This task becomes particularly challenging when the available input states are finite in number, only partially characterized, and may not be identical. Whether there exists a universal purification protocol applicable to such inputs has therefore been a longstanding question. This motivates the study of universal $n$-to-$1$ entanglement purification. Although no such LOCC protocol exists for the full set of two-qubit entangled states, it has remained open whether this no-go result extends to higher-dimensional bipartite states and multipartite states. In this work, we resolve this question by proving that, for any fixed finite local dimensions, no $n$-to-$1$ LOCC protocol is universal for all bipartite entangled states or all multipartite entangled states. We further show that the bipartite and multipartite no-go results persist under several natural extensions and establish an analogous no-go theorem for coherence purification under strictly incoherent operations.

papers.title: The radical pair mechanism can generate nuclear-spin entanglement
papers.abstract: The radical pair mechanism is a quantum-mechanical process underlying weak magnetic field effects in chemical and biological systems. While nuclear polarization and electronic entanglement in this mechanism have been studied extensively, the possibility of creating entanglement between nuclear spins has, to the best of our knowledge, remained unexplored. Here, we show that nuclear-spin entanglement can develop from initially maximally mixed nuclear spin states and evolve over repeated radical pair cycles. Its generation and persistence depend on the initial electronic state, the available reaction channels, and the interplay between recombination rates, hyperfine interactions, and the magnetic field. We demonstrate this behaviour in both a minimal two-nucleus model and a five-nucleus model inspired by the photosynthetic radical pair P700--$A_1$. Radical pair mechanism generated nuclear-spin entanglement offers a potential new resource for quantum technologies and opens avenues for exploring its role in biological systems.

papers.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
papers.abstract: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.

papers.title: Radius decay and boundary polymers: cluster expansion for long-range many-body tilts
papers.abstract: We consider a nearest-neighbor Gibbs measure on a region in $\mathbb{Z}^2$ (e.g., the Ising model) tilted by $\sum_{x,r} g_{x,r}$, where $g_{x,r}$ is an arbitrary function of the spins in the ball of radius $r$ about $x$, with $\|g_{x,r}\|_\infty\leq \exp(-C r)$: an exponential decay in the radius of the ball rather than in its volume. Standard cluster expansions fail for such many-body tilts, as a ball of radius $r$ carries $\exp(c r^2)$ configurations. We show that the partition function can be resummed into a polymer model whose polymers are outer boundaries of connected unions of balls, decorated by the spins along them, with weights decaying exponentially in the boundary length. The proof uses only the domain Markov property of the base measure; it develops a version of this resummation argument that appeared in a recent work of the authors in the context of RG analysis of Grassmann variables. As applications, we show convergent cluster expansions for many-body tilts of Ising models at high and low temperatures; existence of infinite-volume limits; and exponential decay of correlations.

papers.title: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
papers.abstract: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator. In practice, we find that the criterion based on the second-order moments of the realigned operator is already sufficient to witness the entanglement of a wide range of quantum optical states. The realigned moments can be readily accessed using an optical scheme consisting of a linear interferometer that couples several identical copies of the state, similarly to the multicopy technique used to measure the partial-transpose moments of a state [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064 (2026)]. We illustrate the detection capability of the second-order realigned-moment method for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.

papers.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state. The analysis is performed for the DUNE setup and extended beyond its baseline to study the interplay between wave-packet decoherence and matter effects over long distances. For the DUNE baseline, finite wave-packet widths suppress and smooth the oscillations relative to the PW case, with smaller widths causing stronger damping, while matter effects modify the amplitudes and positions of the oscillation features. Among the considered measures, residual $l_1$-norm coherence dominates over the entanglement measures. At very long propagation distances, wave-packet decoherence progressively washes out the oscillatory behavior, driving the oscillation probabilities and quantum correlation measures toward averaged values, with smaller wave-packet widths leading to earlier damping. Further, in the $L-δ_{\rm CP}$ plane, residual $l_1$-norm coherence exhibits weak $δ_{\rm CP}$ dependence, while Concurrence Fill and Three-$π$ entanglement show greater sensitivity at the DUNE baseline. Beyond a characteristic baseline in the extended propagation regime, all three measures approach constant values, independent of $L$ and $δ_{\rm CP}$.

papers.title: Multiconfigurational mixed quantum-classical approach for correlated many-body dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce a multiconfigurational mixed quantum-classical many-body approach for simulating the finite-temperature correlated multi-exciton dynamics in the presence of phonon-induced static and dynamic disorder. In this mixed quantum-classical approach, the excitonic subsystem is des…

papers.title: Information Thermodynamics in Closed Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Although information thermodynamics explains how the second law is modified due to the information acquired by Maxwell's demon, its formulation in many-body systems remains largely open. Here, we develop an information-thermodynamic framework for closed quantum many-body systems initially in microscopic thermal equilibrium (MITE), under physically motivated restrictions: local quantum measurements and finite-time controls generated by local Hamiltonians. By additionally assuming that each local feedback term depends only on nearby measurement outcomes, we rigorously prove that the extractable work coincides in the thermodynamic limit with that extractable from the corresponding canonical ensemble. We further express this extractable work in terms of quantum-information quantities, including the quantum-classical mutual information and the Holevo information for the corresponding canonical ensemble. We also show that feedback based on distant measurement outcomes can exploit long-range correlations hidden in MITE, yielding an extensive increase in extracted work relative to the canonical ensemble.

papers.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
papers.abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction. In this paper, we organize decoding algorithms, execution strategies, and code constructions using common classifications and examine their performance and trade-offs under the reported evaluation conditions. We distinguish decoder-level hierarchy, where multiple decoding stages or resources cooperate to decode a single code, from code-level hierarchy, where the code construction itself introduces multiple decoding levels. We first review single-code hierarchical decoders and their cascaded predecoding and windowed, streaming, and distributed implementations. We then study hierarchical and concatenated codes, focusing on how decoding is coordinated across code levels through hard decisions, soft reliability information, or syndrome information. We also examine how qubit modalities shape decoding workloads and timing requirements, and review how different decoding platforms meet these requirements, including central processing units (CPUs), graphics processing units (GPUs), field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), and cryogenic platforms. By assessing design trade-offs, this paper clarifies connections across the literature and provides a shared foundation for QEC design exploration. It also identifies gaps in performance reporting and system integration to guide future research toward practical quantum error correction.

papers.title: Feedback Control and Neural-Network-Based Prediction of Quantum Entanglement in Fano-mirror cavity optomechanics
papers.abstract: Quantum entanglement involving the centre-of-mass motion of macroscopic-scale objects plays an essential role in both fundamental science and emerging quantum technologies, yet generating and verifying such macroscopic nonclassical states remain formidable challenges. Here, we report a theoretical scheme to effectively generate, manipulate, and predict bipartite optomechanical entanglement based on a Fano-mirror cavity optomechanical system with a coherent feedback loop, where the cavity and Fano optical modes couple through coherent and dissipative interactions. We show that the Fano mirror forms a closed tripartite interaction loop with the cavity and mechanical modes, whereby the quantum interference between direct and indirect interaction pathways substantially enhances the cavity-mechanical entanglement and gives rise to a robust Fano-mechanical entanglement. More importantly, we find that coherent feedback combined with an appropriate optical frequency mismatch can further enhance the entanglement, and a trained supervised feedforward neural network can be used to predict the entanglement magnitude from the readily measurable optical signals, relaxing the requirement of full quantum-state tomography. Our work, establishing an all-optical and experimentally feasible approach to generate, manipulate, and characterize the macroscopic optomechanical entanglement, holds great potential for applications in quantum information processing.

papers.title: Going beyond the standard quasiparticle picture: Entanglement spreading after quenching from highly entangled states
papers.abstract: The quasiparticle picture provides a quantitative description of entanglement spreading after quantum quenches in integrable systems. In interacting models, however, it relies on the assumption that the quench creates entangled pairs of quasiparticles, which is justified only for the so-called integrable initial states. Here we go beyond this setting by studying quenches in the XXZ spin chain from the $n$-rainbow states, a family of macroscopically homogeneous states formed by increasingly long-range Bell pairs, which are not integrable for $n>1$. The local stationary state after the quench approaches the infinite-temperature state as $n\to\infty$, with corrections of order $1/n$, as we show analytically. Nevertheless, in the noninteracting XX chain the quench produces entangled multiplets of $2n$ species of quasiparticles. Although interspecies correlations vanish as $1/n$, they strongly suppress the growth of the entanglement entropy, whose rate vanishes as $n\to\infty$. We capture this behaviour within a generalized quasiparticle picture. In the interacting XXZ chain, instead, time-dependent density matrix renormalization group (tDMRG) simulations show that the entanglement entropy grows at the rate at which thermodynamic entropy is exchanged across the cut. Within the time scales accessible to tDMRG, the data show no trace of the multiplet suppression. This holds both after homogeneous quenches and after joining the $n$-rainbow state with an infinite-temperature state, for which we conjecture a formula for the von Neumann entropy.

papers.title: Full Mesh Dynamic Four-User Entanglement-based Switched QKD Network Integrated with SD-KMS
papers.abstract: We demonstrate a reconfigurable, four-user, full-mesh quantum key distribution network using polarization entanglement, integrated with a software-defined key management system to orchestrate dynamic optical switching and real-time key provisioning for quantum-safe applications.

papers.title: Device-independent witnesses of genuine multipartite entanglement and nonlocality for GHZ states and Bell-pair tree
papers.abstract: We derive and compare device-independent witnesses of genuine multipartite entanglement (GME) and genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL) for GHZ states and trees of Bell pairs. A binary-outcome family using four global measurement contexts has the tight biseparable bound independent of the number of parties. We distinguish these GME bounds from Svetlichny-hybrid bounds, which permit arbitrary communication within either side of a bipartition. For GHZ states, we also give a $2N$-context GMNL witness and compare it with MABK and Svetlichny tests. For Bell-pair trees, sums of CHSH and chained inequalities certify GME and GMNL, respectively, with explicitly specified input protocols and multi-bit local outputs. Separately, we prove the sharp four-context network bound $I_λ\leq2$ for every $N\geq3$ and $λ\geq2$, and bound the MABK scores of quantum networks assembled from bipartite sources. We successfully benchmark MABK, four-context, and Svetlichny witnesses on IBM Quantum GHZ preparations up to $10$ parties, under the local-measurement and sampling assumptions.

papers.title: Connected regular $Γ$-distance magic graphs with magic constant zero
papers.abstract: Let $(Γ,+)$ be a finite Abelian group. A $Γ$-distance magic labeling of a graph is a bijection from its vertex set to $Γ$ such that the sum of the labels of the neighbours of each vertex is a fixed element of $Γ$, called the magic constant. The constructions of Kovář and collaborators provide regular distance magic graphs of odd order with consecutive integer labels for every even degree from $4$ to $14$. We adapt these constructions to prove the existence of connected $r$-regular $(A\times\mathbb{Z}_n)$-distance magic graphs with magic constant $0$, where $A$ is any finite Abelian group of odd order, $n$ is odd, and $r\in\{4,6,8,10,12,14\}$, under explicit sufficient conditions on $n$. Here $\mathbb{Z}_n$ is the cyclic group of order $n$. It suffices to take $n\ge13$ for $r=6$, $n\ge19$ for $r=14$, and $n\ge15$ for $r\in\{4,8,10,12\}$.

papers.title: Towards Distributed Quantum Computing: Quantum Gate Teleportation via Satellite-Distributed Entanglement under Atmospheric Depolarization
papers.abstract: We investigate quantum gate teleportation as a primitive for satellite-enabled distributed quantum computing. In the considered architecture, a satellite distributes entangled photon pairs to two optical ground stations, which transfer the shared quantum resource to remote quantum processing units. This entanglement is then used to implement a nonlocal controlled-NOT gate between two circuit qubits located in different processors. We formulate the minimal four-qubit protocol, consisting of two network qubits that provide the entangled resource and two circuit qubits on which the distributed gate is performed. Atmospheric propagation effects in the gravitational field are modeled through an effective two-qubit depolarizing channel whose parameters depend on atmospheric and optical quantities, including the Fried parameter and receiver aperture. The performance of the protocol is quantified by the fidelity between the ideal CNOT output state and the state produced by noisy quantum gate teleportation. Our results show that the fidelity is governed by the quality of the distributed entanglement and depends jointly on atmospheric coherence, aperture size, and effective depolarization strength. These findings connect physical-layer modeling of satellite optical channels with gate-level performance in distributed quantum computing.

papers.title: Probing Krylov Dynamics in Driven Many-Body Systems
papers.abstract: Krylov complexity has become a central probe of operator growth, scrambling, and quantum chaos. Yet, a basic fact hinders its experimental study: laboratory quantum systems are routinely driven in time, whereas the Krylov construction assumes a fixed generator and breaks down once the Hamiltonian varies. Here, we solve the time-dependent many-body Krylov problem exactly and in closed form for scale- and rotation-invariant systems realized in current quantum-simulation and control platforms. We find exact relations that map the driven dynamics onto mutually orthogonal Krylov subspaces and yield a closed-form spread complexity, determined solely by the spectral properties of the initial Hamiltonian and the driving schedule. The construction extends to Liouville space and solves the time-dependent density-matrix Krylov problem, which makes the Krylov dynamics of initial thermal states experimentally accessible. In scale-invariant quantum gases, such as the driven Lieb-Liniger model, the Tonks-Girardeau gas, and the Calogero-Sutherland model, the complexity is set by the width of the atomic cloud and its rate of change, directly accessible via in situ and time-of-flight imaging. In rotation-invariant spin systems such as the Haldane-Shastry and central-spin models, it is governed by collective spin precession that can be probed and read out in trapped-ion, cavity-QED, and circuit-QED platforms.

papers.title: Long-time behaviour of solutions for equations with randomness
papers.abstract: We discuss results on the mixing properties of solutions for discrete and continuous time equations, drived by stationary bounded random forces, obtained during the last three years in a number or our joint papers. To facilitate applications of these results to specific equations with randomness, the results are edited and properly re-arranged.

papers.title: High-Rate Scalable Entanglement Swapping Between Remote Entanglement Sources on Deployed New York City Fibers
papers.abstract: Performing high-rate entanglement swapping between independent sources over 17.6 km of deployed commercial fiber establishes a scalable architecture for metropolitan quantum networks. [PRX Quantum 7, 043028] Published Tue Nov 10, 2026

papers.title: Integrated infrared photonics with van der Waals polaritonic waveguides
papers.abstract: Integrated photonics has expanded rapidly over the past two decades, driven largely by the demand for high-speed optoelectronic systems in telecommunications and data-center interconnects. Silicon remains the dominant platform, while alternative materials such as thin-film lithium niobate are increa…

papers.title: Symmetric estimator for discrete self-energy of discrete many-body systems
papers.abstract: The self-energy is notoriously difficult to compute, especially in many-body systems with a discrete spectrum, where the Dyson equation often produces noncausal results. Here, the authors obtain a discrete spectral representation of the self-energy that is causal by construction, preserves sum rules, and requires no artificial broadening. Tested with four different impurity solvers, the approach significantly improves accuracy and enables a fully discrete formulation of dynamical mean-field theory.

papers.title: How many events does entanglement-based positronium imaging need? Information limits of Compton polarimetry with CZT detectors
papers.abstract: The degree of polarisation correlation of the two annihilation photons, measured by Compton polarimetry, has been proposed as a PET biomarker of tissue microstructure, but the statistics it requires have not been quantified. We parameterise the measurement by the linear-polarisation correlation coefficient $κ$ ($κ=1$ maximally entangled, $1/2$ separable), derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events and compare it with the quantum Fisher information, relate $κ$ to the annihilation channels of positronium in tissue, and simulate pixelated CdZnTe (CZT) rings. The model is checked against three published measurements and an independent GATE/Geant4 simulation. A double-Compton event carries at most 0.12-0.14 units of Fisher information about $κ$ and 0.015 on average, 0.1-0.6% of the quantum limit. Event-wise maximum likelihood reaches the Cramer-Rao bound, whereas the conventional ratio R needs 1.2-2.3 times more events. The observed coefficient is $κ_{obs}=1-α(1-κ_{pick})$, with a pick-off share $α$ of 0.13-0.29 in tissue; it is sensitive to lipid fraction but not to oxygen, and carries no tissue information if pick-off photons are maximally entangled. Published porous-polymer data imply $κ_{pick}$ = 0.34-0.58. In a 15-mm CZT module, ordering ambiguity, position errors and electron transport roughly halve the information per event, and sequence reconstruction of multi-site events recovers this loss. With $^{18}$F and an eight-module ring, $κ$ can be measured to $\pm0.01$ in a 10-mm tumour, but separating tissues by $κ$ alone requires 6-74 times more decays than are available.

papers.title: Entanglement and Charge Transfer
papers.abstract: We compute the entropic order parameter introduced in (1905.10487) using the replica trick for two disjoint intervals. For a global symmetry, this quantity measures the mutual information carried by charge-anticharge intertwiners. We formulate the problem in terms of averages over twisted partition functions on replica Riemann surfaces, and obtain exact solutions for free fermions and compact bosons, for $U(1)$ symmetry and its discrete $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroups. We show that further averaging over both families of non-contractible cycles gives access to an additional quantity, which is the loss of Holevo information associated with complementary-charge measurements that occurs upon removing the intertwiners. For the boson, this quantity vanishes, whereas for Dirac fermions it equals the difference between the mutual information of the fermion-parity-gauged and ungauged theories, independently of the choice of even $\mathbb Z_N$ subgroup. Finally, we extend the analysis to non-Abelian symmetries using saddle expansions, deriving universal behavior in the nearly touching intervals limit and for a large number of fermions $N_F\gg1$.

papers.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
papers.abstract: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

papers.title: Global Lanczos with stochastic error correction for trace estimation of matrix functions
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for computing the trace of a matrix function $f(A)$, where $A$ is a large, sparse, symmetric matrix. Our approach combines a deterministic global Lanczos approximation with a stochastic correction of its error. Starting the global Lanczos process with the identity matrix yields a direct approximation of the trace through a small tridiagonal matrix. The resulting basis matrices are polynomials in $A$, allowing the process to be implemented using sparse matrix-matrix multiplications when low-degree polynomials in $A$ have moderate fill-in. However, increased fill-in may limit the number of iterations that can be performed efficiently. To address this limitation, we derive an exact representation of the global Lanczos error as the trace of a matrix function and apply a stochastic estimator to the remainder. Even a moderately accurate estimate can substantially improve the accuracy, combining the deterministic method with the rapid initial convergence of stochastic trace estimators. We discuss error bounds and variance reduction, and present numerical experiments that compare the resulting method with existing ones.

papers.title: Quantum Cooling by Classical Shadows
papers.abstract: Cooling to ground states of many-body Hamiltonians by imaginary-time evolution is central to quantum simulation, but its non-unitary aspect prevents direct implementation on a quantum computer. Existing routes restore it by importing structure from outside the intrinsic quantum dynamics, e.g. by parameter estimation on many copies or recursive compilation. Here, we show that a single randomized snapshot of the quantum many-body system is sufficient to steer the state along the cooling direction on average. Our algorithm, shadow chain, uses randomized measurements to collapse the state to its classical record, which fixes the next unitary update. Snapshots across steps form a trajectory that is a quantum-executable sample of an auxiliary-field path integral; fluctuations among trajectories are exponentially suppressed in system size. With the randomness supplied intrinsically by the Born measurement rule, the trajectories sample themselves rather than going through external accept-reject steps. The resulting algorithm is ansatz-free and exact upon extrapolation to the continuous limit, with the exponential cost confined only to system size rather than temperature.

papers.title: Transfer-Matrix Calculus for Infinite Matrix Product States
papers.abstract: Long-range interactions, from the Coulomb repulsion between electrons to the power-law interactions of trapped ions and Rydberg atoms, are widespread in quantum many-body physics. For infinite systems, however, MPS algorithms, the standard classical reference in one dimension, conventionally rely on a computational compromise: replacing these interactions by fitted sums of exponentials. We develop transfer-matrix calculus (TMC), a unified framework for deriving infinite-MPS algorithms. In TMC, an interaction is written as a function of the transfer matrix, and one set of contraction rules then yields the effective Hamiltonians of DMRG and VUMPS, the tangent-space excitation action, and the energy variance, without an MPO. Long-range interactions thus enter with their prescribed distance dependence. For the half-filled lattice Coulomb chain with a $1/d$ interaction of strength $V$, theory predicts CDW order for all $V>0$, but at weak coupling this order is too weak for earlier numerics to resolve. Using TMC, we obtain infinite-MPS ground states at $V=2$ directly in the thermodynamic limit, with an energy variance per site of $2\times10^{-10}$. Our data, extrapolated to zero energy variance, indicate a small nonzero CDW amplitude, $m_0=0.002213(14)$, consistent with this prediction. The complete $V=2$ optimization workflow across the full series of bond dimensions takes less than a day on a single AMD MI250X GPU die. For an exactly solvable long-range hopping model, TMC reproduces the nonanalytic $|k|$ cusp of the one-particle dispersion that any fixed finite sum of decaying exponentials rounds off. We also use TMC to optimize first-quantized MPS directly in the thermodynamic limit. For half-filled free fermions, our entanglement entropy data show scaling consistent with central charge $c=1$ over the studied bond dimensions, as for second-quantized MPS.

papers.title: Fragmentation in non-Hermitian many-body systems
papers.abstract: In non-Hermitian (NH) fermionic chains with spatially random imaginary gauge fields, single-particle eigenstates exhibit erratic NH skin localization with strongly fluctuating, subexponential decay, distinct from both conventional skin accumulation and Anderson localization. At finite filling, Pauli…

papers.title: Communication Supremacy of a Qubit in Holevo Frenkel Weiner Scenario
papers.abstract: The prevailing wisdom asserts that in the Holevo Frenkel Weiner (HFW) framework of communication tasks, a qubit offers no advantage over a c bit unless additional quantum resources are supplied or the classical shared randomness (SR) is restricted. In contrast, we establish the supremacy of qubit communication in the HFW framework when additional quantum resources, such as entanglement or measurement incompatibility are not injected and SR is a free resource. We consider a prepare-measure scenario where the sender, Alice, prepares six states subject to a specific cryptographic constraint, and the receiver, Bob, performs a three-outcome measurement. Such a constraint on preparation impacts the power of qubit communication quite differently than that of c-bit communication, ultimately giving rise to the quantum advantage. We introduce a witness capable of distinguishing quantum strategies that lie beyond the set of possible classical strategies and demonstrate the optimal quantum advantage. {As an application, we demonstrate the generation of certified randomness without requiring any seed randomness, since Bob has no input.} We further analyse the robustness of the witness and show that the advantage persists in noisy situations, making it suitable for experimental realisation. Finally, we demonstrate that Bob's three outcome qubit positive operator valued-measure (POVMs) has a distinct capability of detecting coherence, which can be regarded as the non-classical feature responsible for showcasing the quantum advantage.

papers.title: Infinite or indefinite: the query cost of simulating the quantum switch
papers.abstract: The quantum switch applies two operations in a coherent superposition of their causal orders and is a simple example of indefinite causal order. No quantum circuit that uses each operation once in a definite order can even describe it, yet photonic experiments have demonstrated its physical realization. We ask how many calls to the black-box operations a quantum computer in the circuit model needs to reproduce the switch. If one of the black boxes is known to be unitary, three calls suffice. For general channels on a $d$-dimensional system, we prove three results. In all three, circuits may use classical feed-forward and unlimited ancillary quantum memory. First, no finite number of calls suffices for exact simulation in the worst case. Second, approximation to any fixed error below $1/2$, measured in half the diamond norm, requires $Ω(d^{1/4})$ calls, exponential in the number of qubits. Third, an ordinary circuit can require exponentially many calls to obtain a single bit that the switch extracts with a few uses. We consider a device whose actual noise is dephasing in a fixed unknown basis and test it against a theoretical depolarizing model. The two channels have the same entanglement and average gate fidelities, so these figures alone do not distinguish them. At fixed noise strength, the quantum switch tells them apart with a number of device uses independent of $d$, whereas the circuit model requires $Ω(d^{1/16})$ calls. Noise characterization is needed for quantum error correction, and this gives a provable query advantage of the switch in a task relevant to practical quantum computing. We invite future work that extends such advantages to more practical computing tasks.

papers.title: Enhanced Entanglement Gate Fidelity via Correlated and Synchronized Atom Motion
papers.abstract: Engineered collective dissipation can correlate and even synchronize the motion of quantum systems. We show that such motional correlations can suppress motion-induced errors in two-qubit controlled-phase gates based on the Rydberg blockade in neutral-atom tweezer arrays. To leading order in the Lamb-Dicke parameter, the motional contribution to the gate infidelity is determined solely by the two-atom motional occupations and correlations, and is independent of the gate protocol. We illustrate this result for correlated thermal states and synchronized quantum van der Pol oscillators. In each case, motional correlations reduce the gate infidelity relative to independent thermal atoms at finite temperature. Our results establish atomic-motion correlations as a resource for high-fidelity neutral-atom gates and may also find applications in analog quantum simulators.

papers.title: An Architecture for Real-Time Quantum Error Correction with Neutral Atoms
papers.abstract: The latency of quantum measurement and classical decoding constrains the execution of adaptive fault-tolerant circuits. In neutral-atom processors, this requirement couples spatially resolved fluorescence detection to classical inference. Here we implement cascaded readout and decoding in a heterogeneous architecture that overlaps acquisition and processing at two spatial scales. Field-programmable gate arrays process camera rows as they arrive, while graphics processors decode an acquired logical block during acquisition of the next. This heterogeneous architecture offers flexibility in the choice of error-correcting codes and decoding algorithms. Direct communication preserves microsecond-scale transfer times for kilobyte payloads and supports interchangeable decoding algorithms. Hardware characterization and decoding benchmarks using circuit-level simulated syndromes yield a submillisecond post-exposure processing latency for selected small-code workloads ($d = 3, 5, 7$). By enabling logical blocks to be decoded before full-frame readout is complete, the architecture implements low-latency syndrome decoding, realizing real-time quantum information processing as required for fault-tolerant computation in atom arrays.

papers.title: CSS Circuits: useful quantum circuits that can be simulated with $O(1)$ cost per gate
papers.abstract: "CSS circuits" are quantum circuits generated by $X$, $Z$, $M_X$, $M_Z$, and CNOT gates. Although CSS circuits are extremely restrictive, they can implement important quantum protocols like teleportation, error correction, and entanglement purification. We present a simple CSS circuit simulator that uses $O(1)$ work per gate. The simulator corresponds to a local hidden variable model, so we use Bell inequalities to prove the simulator can't also support Hadamard gates, CZ gates, or S gates. We note that CSS circuits appear ideal for benchmarking quantum error correction in the presence of atom loss errors.

papers.title: Approximate error correction for quantum simulations of SU(2) lattice gauge theories
papers.abstract: We present a protocol for actively suppressing Gauss law violations in quantum simulations of SU(2) lattice gauge theory. Mid-circuit measurements extract a syndrome (J,M,N) characterizing the gauge-violation sector at each vertex by resolving both the total angular momentum and the magnetic quantum…

papers.title: Many-Body-Driven Ultrafast Exciton Relaxation Enabled by Phonon-Activated Coulomb Coupling
papers.abstract: Coulomb interactions underpin the formation of excitons, yet their role in nonequilibrium exciton relaxation has remained unexplored. Here, using first-principles real-time Bethe-Salpeter formalism combined with nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, we study the ultrafast relaxation of optically bright e…

papers.title: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
papers.abstract: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the Hölder continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics. The novelty of our approach allows for the study of such properties notwithstanding the lack of a spectral gap for the corresponding transition operator.

papers.title: Localization transition in a spin chain with an exact Fock-space tree
papers.abstract: Many-body localization is often pictured as Anderson localization on the graph of many-body configurations. Strongly correlated disorder and a dense net of loops, however, make this graph hard to analyze. We introduce a local disordered spin-1 chain in which a single domain wall explores an exact binary tree of configurations. Random fields create strongly correlated disorder on this tree, as in generic interacting systems, while the absence of loops keeps the problem tractable. We rigorously bound the spreading of the domain wall at strong disorder, and efficient numerics on exponentially large trees indicate a localization transition at finite disorder strength.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning designs Quantum Repeater Protocols on Networks beyond the Chain Scenario
papers.abstract: Small-scale quantum repeater protocols have been shown to distribute entanglement over existing telecommunication infrastructure by means of short range quantum communications and long range classical messages. For larger networks, there are a number of theoretical proposals about how to operate the network to achieve a good performance under varying metrics. Moreover, since the dimension of the space of possible protocols grows exponentially with network size, plenty of those proposals are based on heuristics that reduce the search space. One of these is entanglement routing, which simplifies the problem on non-linear networks by allocating a series of disjoint paths and running chain protocols simultaneously on them. However, in this work we claim routing leads to suboptimal protocols. In fact, inspired by works on linear chains, we apply reinforcement learning to non-linear networks and optimize over the larger non-routing protocol space. Then, we find protocols that outperform a routed extension of the swap-ASAP protocol, even in the parameter regimes where the latter is widely recognized as the state of the art. These results indicate that routing must be discarded in favor of non-routing methods, while they pave the way towards the design of a sensible Quantum Internet architecture.

papers.title: What kind of quantum advantage is this?
papers.abstract: Quantum advantage encompasses fundamentally different claims, from resource reductions to exponential separations in sample complexity. Evaluating these claims requires distinguishing how an algorithm achieves an advantage from what is necessary for the separation and how strongly it is supported against classical alternatives. We propose a multi-label taxonomy that makes these distinctions explicit, classifying structural, interference, and coherent mechanisms while separately recording their necessity and the evidence for the classical comparison.
