The notes also discuss the passage to the exceptional set estimates for orthogonal projections, the exclusion of Borel subrings of intermediate Hausdorff dimension, and Fourier decay for multiplicative convolutions of measures.

papers.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with super critical viscosity
papers.abstract: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

papers.title: Observable Spectral Framework for Noisy Amplitude Amplification: Stopping Stability and Correction
papers.abstract: Stopping rules for noisy amplitude amplification often rely on channel-specific success-probability formulas, limiting their transfer across noise mechanisms. We develop an observable spectral framework for stationary noisy standard amplitude amplification under explicit leading-mode, spectral-separation, and residual-control conditions. Within this class, the first amplification lobe has a damped-oscillatory leading component and a bounded non-leading contribution. We derive how frequency shift, damping, and observable phase offset displace the leading peak, and establish sampled-gap criteria for retaining the ideal integer stopping depth, certifying recalibration, or selecting a robust candidate window. In single-target Grover search, frequency and damping errors have stopping-coordinate sensitivities proportional to the search-space size, whereas phase offsets scale with its square root; residual modes can independently reverse the ordering of neighbouring depths. Analytical constructions, circuit simulations, finite-shot inference, and calibration-derived device-like trajectories examine these predictions and their operational limits. For a 64-element search, an a posteriori sampled-set check selects depth five over six, with success probability increasing from 0.595 to 0.626. The resulting theory links observable spectral dynamics to conditional integer stopping guarantees without requiring a separate microscopic channel solution.

papers.title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
papers.abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $κ$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{π_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in (arXiv:2404.12607), and verify a conjecture of the second author in (arXiv:2604.11958) in the rank $2$ case.

papers.title: Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains
papers.abstract: For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains. The usual connected form cannot hold exactly for geometric chains; we determine its exact form, show that it holds modulo gluing and covering relations in a complex computing the homology of the moduli spaces, and that the vertex currents are the unique top-dimensional solution. Finally we compare with Costello's homotopical framework. In a strict model given by hyperbolic surfaces with marked boundary points, every solution of his master equation with his initial condition integrates exactly to the vertex currents, up to the sign (-1)^(3g-3+n); such solutions exist, are unique up to homotopy, and correspond to the hyperbolic vertices. Under a continuity assumption on the comparison map and granting the inputs of Costello's homology computation, the hyperbolic vertices represent his homotopy class of solutions, for a completed notion of homotopy.

papers.title: Noise-Aware Testing of NISQ Quantum Programs: Self-Baseline Oracle with a Controlled False-Positive Rate
papers.abstract: Testing quantum programs on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices faces a test-oracle problem: hardware noise and finite-shot sampling make the runs of a correct program vary as much as those of a faulty one, so oracles with a fixed acceptance threshold produce false positives that depend on the program and the backend. We present a noise-aware testing framework built on self-baseline calibration: each run of the program under test is compared with repeated executions of a trusted reference program on the same backend, and the acceptance threshold is the $(1-α)$ quantile of the finite-shot null distribution of the Jensen-Shannon divergence, so the oracle's false-positive rate is a level set in advance. A noncentral chi-square model predicts detection power, a homogeneity test and a two-run sentinel detect drift, a mutation engine labels every mutant exactly within a three-class noise-aware taxonomy, and zero-noise extrapolation attributes rejections to faults or noise. In simulation on nine core benchmarks, 32 QASMBench programs, ten real bugs, seven noise regimes and three device snapshots, the oracle's false-positive rate is 0.0011 at $α= 10^{-3}$ over 9,000 correct runs, against 36-74% for fixed thresholds, 8.9% for a QOIN-style filter and 10.8% for a globally calibrated threshold, while attaining the highest F1 on non-equivalent faults (0.941). On an IBM Heron device, using about 14 minutes of QPU time, it rejected none of 82 correct runs and detected 120 of 121 faults and semantic mutants, and a two-run sentinel reduced drift-induced false positives from 27.4% to 1.8%.

papers.title: Folding of d-invariants via F-invariants with applications to quiver Hecke KR-modules
papers.abstract: The \(\de\)-invariant measures the interaction between two simple modules and controls the behavior of their convolution product. Using categorical interpretations of Cao's tropical and \(F\)-invariants, we establish folding formulas for the \(Λ\)-invariants between determinantial modules in arbitrary symmetrizable type and derive the corresponding \(\de\)-formula by symmetrization. We apply the \(\de\)-formula to quiver Hecke Kirillov--Reshetikhin modules and show that, in every finite type, their \(\de\)-invariants are completely determined by the coefficients of the symmetrized inverse \(t\)-quantized Cartan matrix. We obtain explicit formulas in all finite types, including closed formulas in the classical types \(A\), \(B\), \(C\), and \(D\).

papers.title: Quantum Sensor of Mechanical Vibrations
papers.abstract: We report the use of a single trapped-ion motional mode as a probe of mechanical vibrations of the Paul trap structure. By exciting vibrations of the trap using an ultrasonic transducer mounted outside the vacuum chamber and probing the ion motion through motional sideband interactions, we observe a clear resonance response of the axial mode. We further demonstrate detection of trap vibrations with amplitudes as low as 0.6 picometers. These measurements show direct coupling between macroscopic mechanical motion and trapped-ion dynamics, providing a route toward vibration sensing using quantum control of motional states.

papers.title: A new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a new class of Manin triples of compatible Lie algebras and investigates the corresponding bialgebra structures. To this end, we first study an invariant-c$2$c form on a compatible Lie algebra, namely a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form that is invariant with respect to one Lie bracket and is a commutative $2$-cocycle with respect to the other, which naturally arises from a quadratic differential Novikov algebra. Then we introduce the notion of compatible Lie-anti-pre-Lie algebras (compatible LAPL algebras in short), which serve as the underlying algebra structures of compatible Lie algebras endowed with invariant-c$2$c forms. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a compatible LAPL bialgebra, which is shown to be equivalent to a Manin triple of compatible Lie algebras with respect to the invariant-c$2$c form. We investigate triangular compatible LAPL bialgebras, which are obtained from antisymmetric solutions of the compatible LAPL Yang-Baxter equation. We also use $\mathcal{O}$-operators of compatible LAPL algebras to construct such solutions. Finally, we show that every differential Novikov bialgebra gives rise to a compatible LAPL bialgebra and that this construction preserves triangularity.

papers.title: Liouville theorems for nonlinear polyharmonic equations with indefinite nonlinearities
papers.abstract: We establish a Liouville theorem for nonnegative bounded solutions of the indefinite polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=x_1u^p$ in $\mathbb R^n$, for all integers $m\ge2$, $n\ge1$, and all $p>1$. The main difficulty lies in extending the moving-plane method to a higher-order equation with a sign-changing coefficient. We first combine sublinear growth estimates with reflection arguments to establish the super-polyharmonic property in the right half-space, without prescribing boundary conditions on the separating hyperplane. We then use a doubling and rescaling argument to obtain relative first- and second-derivative estimates on strips, replacing the scalar Harnack estimates used in the second-order case. These estimates allow us to establish monotonicity in the $x_1$-direction within the right half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, and a cutoff argument then yields the desired nonexistence result.

papers.title: Full $t$-Linkage, Cancellation, and Almost Krull Domains
papers.abstract: Motivated by open questions of Kabbaj and Mimouni, we determine the position of full $t$-linkage among the standard classes of integral domains and its relationship with almost Krullness. Full linkage for a star operation is equivalent to cancellation in the monoid of all nonzero fractional star ideals. For the $t$-operation, this full cancellation law, denoted by $\mathrm{TCL}$, lies strictly between the $t$-almost Dedekind and completely integrally closed classes; on the $\mathrm{PvMD}$ locus, we recover the known $t$-almost Dedekind characterization. We prove that $\mathrm{TCL}$ and almost Krullness are incomparable. A monoid algebra arising from Reinhart's example satisfies $\mathrm{TCL}$ but is neither almost Krull nor a $\mathrm{PvMD}$. In the opposite direction, we construct a locally factorial almost Krull domain with a maximal ideal $0\ne M=M_t=(M^2)_t\subsetneq D$. For this domain the canonical locally divisorial operation $κ$ is cancellative and $κ_f=t$, but cancellation does not descend to $t$. In contrast, finite valuation patching proves that the Heinzer--Ohm and Arnold--Matsuda almost Krull non-$\mathrm{PvMD}$s satisfy $\mathrm{TCL}$ with $t<κ$; in the latter example $κ=v$. Class-monoid, residual, and support criteria identify the obstruction to descent. Thus the missing $t$-linkage node is governed by cancellation in the entire fractional $t$-ideal monoid, rather than by local Krullness alone.

papers.title: Neural Operator Approximation for Yau--Yau Nonlinear Filtering: Stability, Approximation, and Fast Computation
papers.abstract: Since the introduction of the Kalman filter, nonlinear state estimation has become an important topic in areas such as aerospace engineering, sensor design, and target tracking. Within the optimal filtering framework described by the Duncan-Mortensen-Zakai (DMZ) equation, Yau-Yau filtering (YYF) employs an offline-online decomposition: the Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov (FKE) equations, initialized by a prescribed set of basis functions, are solved offline, and the prior density is projected onto these basis functions during the online stage. However, this approach still faces two computational challenges: solving multiple FKEs offline can be computationally expensive, and the online projection becomes costly when filtering is performed repeatedly or in high-dimensional settings. To address these limitations, we develop a neural operator filter (NOF) that directly learns the mapping from the prior density to the posterior density, thereby eliminating both the expensive offline FKE solves and the online projection. The underlying operator is approximated using a Fourier neural operator (FNO). Numerical experiments on several challenging filtering systems verify both the effectiveness and accuracy of our method, and we further provide a rigorous theoretical analysis of its stability and approximation error.

papers.title: Solutions concentrating on spheres for Hamiltonian elliptic systems with supercritical growth
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of the singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -\varepsilon^2Δu+u=|v|^{q-2}v &\text{in }A,\\ -\varepsilon^2Δv+v=|u|^{p-2}u &\text{in }A,\\ u,v>0\text{ in }A,\qquad u=v=0 &\text{on }\partial A, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $A=\{x\in\mathbb R^{2m}:a<|x|<b\}$, $0<a<b$, $m\geq2$, and $2<p,q<2(m+1)/(m-1)$. We prove the existence of a family of solutions whose two components concentrate around the same $(m-1)$-dimensional sphere on the inner boundary as $\varepsilon\to0$. The two spheres of maxima are at distance $o(\varepsilon)$ from each other, and both components decay exponentially away from these spheres. The admissible range of $(p,q)$ includes critical and supercritical exponent pairs in dimension $2m$. The proof uses a reduction to a weighted system in dimension $m+1$. We establish foliated Schwarz symmetry of its ground states with a common axis via reduction by inversion and polarization. A uniform estimate on generalized Nehari fibers gives the upper energy bound. A half-space nonexistence result and the corresponding lower bound then determine the concentration location and the limiting profiles.

papers.title: Finite-time blowup in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics model
papers.abstract: We prove finite-time blowup of both the velocity and magnetic field in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) model starting from smooth odd initial data. The construction combines the dynamical rescaling approach with weighted stability estimates. Both the velocity and magnetic field remain in $L^2$ before the blowup time.

papers.title: Distribution of Primes in Galois Extensions of Global Fields with Explicit Constant Terms
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of primes among Frobenius conjugacy classes in finite Galois extensions of global fields. In earlier work, the author and Koyama proved that the existence and nonvanishing of the limit of partial Euler products on the critical line for Artin $L$-functions (the Deep Riemann Hypothesis (A), or DRH(A)) are equivalent to an asymptotic formula for weighted prime counting functions with an unspecified constant term. In this article, we prove that a refined asymptotic formula is equivalent to the full version of DRH, namely the convergence of the Euler products on the critical line (DRH(A)) and the determination of their limiting values (DRH(B)). Here, the constant term is given explicitly in terms of the residue of the zeta function, central derivatives of Artin $L$-functions, ramified primes, and higher prime-power contributions.

papers.title: $G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds
papers.abstract: Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of Kędzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities. Combined with known results, this shows that for every three-dimensional canonical abelian quotient singularity, the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities, every essential divisor over the singularity appears on it as a prime divisor, and its limit F-blowup is a resolution of the singularity. These results also hold for every three-dimensional $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial canonical toric singularity in any characteristic, if we replace the $G$-Hilbert scheme by the limit F-blowup of the singularity.

papers.title: Relaxation Critical Dynamics of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) is unique to mixed states: strong symmetry is broken while weak symmetry is preserved, requiring two order parameters. We study the critical relaxation of both order parameters in a monitored $\mathbb{Z}_2$ circuit, which maps exactly onto two nested bond-percolation problems. The initial state acts as a temporal boundary condition for each problem, wired if the state is ordered in the corresponding order parameter and free otherwise. An SW-SSB initial state wires only the strong-symmetry order parameter, a configuration that no pure state realizes. Each autocorrelation exponent is the sum of an initial scaling dimension, set by the initial state, and an observation dimension, set by the observation time, whereas the equal-time correlator gives only the observation dimension. For the SW-SSB state, the initial dimension is $1/3$ for the weak-symmetry order parameter and $0$ for the strong-symmetry one, each at its own critical point. These initial dimensions also set how fast a stored bit is lost. The probability of decoding the initial value of a single qubit from the system alone decays as a power law, whereas system and environment together retain it. Stabilizer simulations confirm the theoretical prediction, and we propose an experimental protocol that measures these exponents without postselection. Our results reveal a form of boundary criticality inaccessible to pure states.

papers.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for the Two-Dimensional Compressible Flow with General Bulk Viscosity
papers.abstract: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for large initial data allowing vacuum. Both the periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with far-field vacuum are considered under a common logarithmic derivative bound and growth condition on the viscosity primitive. A time-independent density upper bound and uniform low-order estimates are obtained in both domains. The admissible coefficients include every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. Exponential relaxation to the positive equilibrium is proved in the periodic setting. In the whole space, uniform relaxation toward vacuum and algebraic decay of the pressure, velocity gradient, material acceleration, and relative kinetic energy are established.

papers.title: Nonsense rank correlations between independent random walks
papers.abstract: Yule's nonsense correlation persists for Spearman's rho and Kendall's tau between independent random walks. Neither coefficient concentrates at zero as the sample size grows. For centred random walks with finite increment variances, we derive a universal joint limit expressed through Brownian occupation functionals. Integral formulas give limiting variances of approximately 0.222 and 0.108, respectively, below the Pearson value of 0.241. Rank correlations thus reduce the limiting dispersion on their respective coefficient scales. We prove that both marginal limits have symmetric densities and represent them exactly as limits of polynomial densities determined by Gaussian moment integrals. Spearman's conventional t test and Kendall's normal approximation are asymptotically invalid, with rejection probabilities tending to one under process independence.

papers.title: Stability threshold of Couette flow for two-dimensional MHD equations on the infinite channel
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the stability threshold of the two-dimensional incompressible MHD equations near Couette flow and a constant horizontal magnetic field \((β,0)\) on \(\mathbb T\times\mathbb R\). For \(N>10\), \(0<ν,μ\le1\) and \(|β|\ge(ν+μ)/(3\sqrt{νμ})\), we prove global stability for initial perturbations of size \(δ_N\min\{ν,μ\}^{1/3}\) in \(H^N\), where \(δ_N>0\) is independent of \(ν,μ,β\). We also obtain enhanced dissipation of the nonzero horizontal modes on the time scale \(\min\{ν,μ\}^{-1/3}\), together with inviscid damping of the vertical components. The proof combines time-dependent Fourier multipliers with an energy correction constructed using the Alfvén oscillations. By combining the nonlinear terms arising from this correction, we obtain the cancellation needed to close the energy estimates at the $1/3$ scale.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Neural Time-Stepping for Gradient-Flow PDEs via Onsager's Variational Principle
papers.abstract: We propose a unified Onsager-based neural time-stepping (ONTS) framework for solving gradient-flow partial differential equations with conserved and nonconserved dynamics. Unlike conventional neural time-stepping methods that directly parameterize the evolving state, the proposed framework employs spatial neural networks to approximate the Onsager process variables, namely, the rates in nonconserved systems and the fluxes in conserved systems. Within this Eulerian framework, we develop three complementary schemes: an explicit least-squares scheme (E-ONTS), an implicit variational scheme (I-ONTS), and a predictor--corrector scheme (PC-ONTS) that combines explicit prediction with safeguarded implicit correction. For conserved systems, the flux-based formulation guarantees discrete mass conservation under periodic or no-flux boundary conditions. Furthermore, we rigorously establish unconditional discrete energy stability for the implicit schemes, provided that a suitable descent criterion is satisfied, without requiring global minimization of the neural variational objective. Numerical experiments for the heat, Allen--Cahn, Cahn--Hilliard, Fokker--Planck, and coupled Poisson--Nernst--Planck equations demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and structure-preserving properties of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Schauder bases and local unconditional structure in Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
papers.abstract: We prove that among the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series with $1\le p<\infty$, only $\mathcal{H}^2$ has local unconditional structure. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}^p$ admits an unconditional basis exactly when $p=2$. At the endpoint $p=1$, we also construct a Schauder basis of Dirichlet polynomials and give an explicit formula for each basis vector. Together, these results answer the basis questions posed by Aleman, Olsen and Saksman, as well as the question of Saksman and Seip concerning an unconditional basis for $\mathcal{H}^1$.

papers.title: A Staggered Discontinuous Galerkin Neural Network Method with a Computable Error Decomposition
papers.abstract: We develop a staggered discontinuous Galerkin neural network (SDGNN) method for scalar elliptic problems with a computable error decomposition. The staggered discontinuous Galerkin (SDG) method requires only local continuity of its trial functions and gives a square, inf-sup stable system without stabilization parameters; we carry this structure over to neural networks. Networks defined on the patches of a staggered mesh satisfy the SDG continuity conditions for all values of the network parameters, and the loss is the squared dual norm of the SDG weak residual. We show that the loss is equivalent, with computable constants, to the square of the training error, the distance between the SDG projection of the network and the SDG finite element approximation, so that the full error is bounded by the discretization error, a multiple of the square root of the loss, and the network projection error. The weak residual requires no derivatives of the networks, the boundary and convection terms carry no penalty or stabilization weights, and the scalar trial functions may jump across the midlines of the primal cells. Numerical experiments show that the square root of the loss tracks the error during the training, that prescribed jumps across a square and a circular interface are captured consistently over the initializations, and that the method is more accurate than physics-informed neural networks at the same parameter counts.

papers.title: $L$-systems on the large Witt design
papers.abstract: Let $L=\{0,1,2,3,4,8\}$, associated with the large Witt design $S(5,8,24)$, and let $m(n,24,L)$ be the maximum size of a family of $24$-element subsets of an $n$-element set whose distinct members have intersection sizes in $L$. We prove that there are positive constants $c,C,n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, \[ cn^{316/63}\leq m(n,24,L)\leq Cn^{169/29}. \] We also obtain similar results for the systems associated with $S(4,7,23)$, $S(3,6,22)$, and $S(3,4,14)$. The upper bounds follow from a non-Shannon information inequality and disprove conjectures of Kupavskii and Terekhov. The lower bounds follow from an algebraic construction for arbitrary Steiner systems.

papers.title: A compact non-Kähler shrinking Ricci soliton
papers.abstract: We construct a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton on the simply-connected eight-manifold $\mathsf{SU}(3)\times_{\mathsf T^2}\mathbb{CP}^1$. This Riemannian manifold is not Einstein, is nowhere locally Kähler, is locally irreducible, and is invariant under the effective cohomogeneity one action of $\mathsf{PSU}(3)\times S^1$. This new gradient Ricci soliton is found by first constructing an approximate solution, certifying the residual, and applying a fixed-point theorem.

papers.title: ECPack.wl: A Mathematica Package for Elliptic Curves over the Rationals and Finite Fields
papers.abstract: We present a Mathematica package entitled ECPack.wl, where we implement many important properties and commands relevant to the study of elliptic curves over the rationals and finite fields, namely $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $q=p^r$ and $p$ is prime. By streamlining the analysis of general elliptic curves and their transformations, ECPack.wl offers foundational computational tools for applications in high-energy physics, including elliptic Feynman integrals. This package significantly extends the functionalities of a package due to McGee in so far as we are able to study all versions of elliptic curves, such as the long Weierstrass, quartic and Legendre forms. We implement suitable transformations that are required for the general case, as well as those associated with fields of characteristic 2 and 3. Furthermore, the package computes many curve properties, such as point arithmetic, minimality checks, rank bounds and analytic rank, group structure, invariants, and the Weil and Tate pairings, over both $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{F}_p$, as well as the Kodaira classification of the singular fibres of one-parameter families of elliptic curves, with the associated F-theory data. The package and its accompanying notebooks are available at https://github.com/DhamakedarDarsh/Mathematica-Code-and-worked-out-notebooks-for-Elliptic-Curves

papers.title: Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$
papers.abstract: We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure. For the Klein four-group with $\underline{\mathbb F}_2$-coefficients, a balanced defect allows us to move $S^V\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ by certain $RO(G)$-graded cohomology classes to its $\dim V$-slice, which is again a representation sphere, while an odd defect obstructs any spherical slice. As an application, we obtain closed formulas for the bottom slice of $Σ^nH\underline{\mathbb{F}}_2$ for every $n$, recovering the computation of Guillou and Yarnall by a different method. Along the way, we determine the complete slice tower of $S^{\inftyα_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$ and consequently, the partial tower for $S^{nα_i}\wedge H\underline{\mathbb F}_2$.

papers.title: Hyperspectral imaging from diffractograms
papers.abstract: We consider an optical system with a periodic point spread function, such as a camera with a periodic diffractive filter array placed near the sensor. Such systems produce a monochrome image that we call ``diffractogram'', and that multiplexes the spatial and spectral information about the scene. We present a method to efficiently invert this forward model and recover the hyperspectral scene. The inverse problem is formulated as a large scale $\ell_1$-penalized least squares problem that is solved iteratively with the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM). A Krylov subspace solver, such as LSQR, may require tens to hundreds of iterations to approximatively solve the augmented least-squares problem required in each ADMM iteration. Here we present an exact direct solver for the augmented least-squares problems that exploits the periodicity of the point spread function. Each direct solve costs roughly as much as three LSQR iterations, eliminating inner iterations entirely. We validate the method on both synthetic and experimental datasets.

papers.title: Limit theorems and bias correction for the initial-noise-adjusted SIML estimator
papers.abstract: We propose a sine-based modification of the separating information maximum likelihood (SIML) estimator for integrated volatility and covariance under equidistant sampling with microstructure noise. The estimator allows for nonzero initial observation noise. We establish consistency under moment assumptions and asymptotic normality under first-order Malliavin regularity of the diffusion coefficients. We also construct a feasible noise-bias correction using an estimator of the unknown noise covariance. This correction permits wider spectral bandwidths for consistency and stable asymptotic normality.

papers.title: Graph Intersections and Hypergraph Discrepancy
papers.abstract: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices with $e(G)=p\binom{n}{2}$ and $e(H)=q\binom{n}{2}$, where $p,q\in(0,1)$ are fixed. Bollobás and Scott studied intersections of two graphs under random relabelling and asked for the minimum $L^2$ norm of the deviation of their intersection size from its expected value. We answer this question by proving that, for graphs of order $n$ with fixed edge densities $p,q\in(0,1)$, the minimum is \begin{equation*} \left(\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)q(1-q)}{2}\cdot\frac{1-\sqrt R}{1+\sqrt R}}\right)n+o(n), \end{equation*} where $R=\max\{p,1-p,q,1-q\}$. The coefficient of the linear term is best possible. Bollobás and Scott defined the positive and negative discrepancies of two hypergraphs as the largest deviations of their intersection size above and below its expected value under relabelling, respectively. They asked for the minimum product of the positive and negative discrepancies of two $(n/2)$-uniform hypergraphs on $n$ vertices with $\frac{1}{2}\binom{n}{n/2}$ edges. We answer this question by proving that the minimum product of these discrepancies is $0$ if $4\mid\binom{n}{n/2}$ and $1/4$ otherwise.

papers.title: Uniqueness for an inverse problem of determining orders and coefficients for multi-term time-fractional diffusion equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a uniqueness problem for determining all fractional orders and their corresponding coefficients in multi-term time-fractional diffusion equations with Caputo derivatives in an abstract Hilbert space. The main result establishes that these parameters can be uniquely identified from a single scalar observation of the solution, of the form (u(t), phi), by comparing the solutions of two evolution equations governed by possibly different positive self-adjoint operators A and B. In contrast to existing results that rely on local space-time measurements and, in particular, may require the initial data to satisfy sign conditions and strong spatial regularity assumptions, our approach uses only the minimal assumption that a belongs to H, without imposing any sign or additional smoothness conditions on the initial value. The proof combines spectral representations of the solutions with a recursive asymptotic comparison method based on fundamental identities for the multinomial Mittag-Leffler function. This approach enables the successive identification of all fractional orders and their associated coefficients, even when the two equations involve different operators. Furthermore, the uniqueness argument extends to multi-term time-fractional wave equations with orders in the interval (1,2).

papers.title: Global existence of an initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation via a Hamiltonian approach
papers.abstract: The global existence of the initial boundary value problem for the Einstein equation in \((2+1)\)-dimension with totally geodesic timelike boundary is proved by a Hamiltonian approach. The initial boundary value problem is formulated within the framework of the ADM formalism, and the ADM reduction is carried out under the constant mean curvature spatial harmonic gauge. Deriving energy estimates for the flows in the reduced phase space shows the global existence.

papers.title: Freidlin-Wentzell exit-laws for a stochastic Cucker-Smale model
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the exit-time asymptotics, at a vanishing noise limit, related to a stochastic particles system in mean-field interaction subjected to frictions, confining potential and flocking forces. The dynamics are governed by a kinetic Langevin-type SDE with an idiosyncratic noise acting solely on the velocity coordinates. Using the seminal large deviations principles of Freidlin and Wentzell [20], and their extension by Azencott [4] to the framework of non-elliptic diffusions, we establish the Arrhenius' law and Kramers' type law related to the first exit-time of the system from an energy level set $\mathcal O^γ_N(R)$ of interest.

papers.title: Effects of elasticity on the stability of viscoelastic boundary layers
papers.abstract: The elastic effect on the stability of boundary layers is studied for incompressible elastic fluids in the half-plane. It is known from [33] that if the deformation tensor matrix is nonsingular near the boundary, elasticity can prevent the formation of a boundary layer. In this paper, we prove stability properties when the deformation tensor degenerates. Our results are twofold: (1) when the first row of the deformation tensor has a non-degenerate projection onto a fixed direction, the initial-boundary value problem for the two-dimensional viscoelastic Prandtl boundary layer equations in the half-plane admits local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces, without any monotonicity condition on the velocity profile; (2) when the first row of the deformation tensor vanishes simultaneously at one point, the linearized Prandtl boundary layer system is ill-posed. The first result reveals the stabilizing effect of elasticity against the classical Prandtl instability. The second result shows that elastic effects cannot suppress the Prandtl-type instability associated with a non-degenerate critical point of the velocity profile.

papers.title: Degenerate Preconditioned Proximal Point Algorithms as Forward Methods for Nonmonotone Inclusions
papers.abstract: We study degenerate preconditioned proximal point algorithms (PPPA) for finding zeros of nonmonotone set-valued operators in Hilbert spaces under solution-relative $(U,V)$-semimonotonicity, with possibly indefinite $U$ and $V$. With a closed-range preconditioner $P$, the reduced PPPA dynamics admit a forward representation through the complementary resolvent of a parallel composition, without requiring monotonicity or admissibility. Relative semimonotonicity of the range-restricted operator transfers to the reduced forward map, allowing our forward theory for possibly set-valued mappings to yield Fejér estimates and residual rates. Under suitable conditions, including demiclosedness of the reduced map at zero, the projected PPPA iterates and shadows converge weakly to a common projected zero. Without demiclosedness, a counterexample shows that the projected sequences may converge to a point outside the projected zero set, even when the original operator is continuous. Bounded recovery condition yields weak convergence of the full (non-projected) shadows. The monotonicity modulus $U$ yields additional results: under suitable conditions, $U\succeqτP$ with $τ>0$ gives strong and linear convergence of the projected PPPA sequences, while $U\succeq-σP$ with $0\leσ<1/2$ still permits local linear rates under metric subregularity. These strong convergence and linear rate guarantees extend to the full shadows when a Lipschitz recovery estimate holds, such as when $U$ is strongly monotone on $\ker P$. For Chambolle--Pock and Douglas--Rachford splitting, we establish Lipschitz recovery even when $U=0$ by exploiting the primal--dual structure. Under suitable parameter conditions, full-shadow convergence guarantees, including $R$-linear rates, extend to the original PPPA iterates.

papers.title: Postselection on Halting and Reductions to the Halting Problem
papers.abstract: A probabilistic Turing machine is an ordinary Turing machine that may also toss fair coins, with no limit on its running time or memory. If it always halts, it decides only computable problems. Aaronson et al. studied machines that may run forever on some coin tosses, with the answer read only from the runs that halt. Suppose the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one. They showed that these machines decide exactly the problems solvable with a fixed list of questions about the halting problem. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be the more likely one. We show that the machines then decide exactly the problems solvable by asking such questions one after another, each chosen after the earlier answers. We also show that the factor two can be replaced by any fixed factor greater than one. A machine may promise two numbers: a lower bound on its probability of halting, and a lower bound on its probability of being right when it halts. From these two numbers we compute exactly how many questions fixed in advance the machine can replace. The main idea is that probability acts as a budget for how often a computable guess may change its mind. The results extend to oracle machines and to machines nested inside each other. Quantum machines decide the same problems.

papers.title: Lieb-Robinson Bounds for Electric Quantum Walks
papers.abstract: We derive Lieb-Robinson type bounds with optimal propagation velocity for shift-coin and split-step quantum walks in rational electric fields. The velocity decays exponentially fast in the period of the field, showing long intervals of suppressed spreading. The proof rests on bounds for the imaginary part of the analytically continued dispersion relation of the electric walk. We show that the infimal Lieb-Robinson velocity coincides with the asymptotic velocity for these walks, while a nonhomogeneous example demonstrates that the two types of velocity need not agree in general. We also obtain an exponential tail estimate on the probability of a walk to lie outside the effective light cone.

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Quantizers for Periodically Time-Varying Systems via Cyclic Reformulation
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the design of optimal dynamic quantizers for discrete-time linear periodically time-varying (LPTV) plants with discrete-valued inputs. Optimal dynamic quantizers, which minimize the worst-case output error caused by quantization, are well established for linear time-invariant (LTI) plants, whereas the corresponding design for plants with periodically time-varying dynamics has not been addressed. For square LPTV plants having relative degree one at every time phase, this paper derives an optimal periodic dynamic quantizer in closed form. The quantizer is constructed by applying the LTI theory to the cycled plant obtained by cyclic reformulation and reading off its periodic coefficient matrices block by block; its optimality is then verified directly, showing that it attains a performance lower bound determined by the largest instantaneous input-to-output gain over the time phases. The worst-case output error of general periodic dynamic quantizers is also characterized. The optimal quantizer is shown to be stable if and only if all invariant zeros of the cycled plant lie in the open unit disk, which is the condition that governs stable causal inversion of LPTV plants. A numerical example with comparisons to conventional quantizers illustrates the results.

papers.title: Decomposition Bounds for MCMC with Mixture Targets: Multimodality and Heavy-Tailedness
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative mixing-time bounds for Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithms targeting multimodal and heavy-tailed mixtures. The dynamics of a Markov chain are decomposed into local and global levels, and possibly weak Poincaré inequalities at both levels are combined to form convergence bounds. We apply this framework to location and scale mixtures of strongly log-concave distributions, obtaining explicit convergence bounds for random-walk Metropolis, proximal, and random-scan Gibbs samplers. For location mixtures connected along a finite path, the bounds depend polynomially on the number of components and exponentially on neighboring separation, remaining informative as the overall diameter grows. For scale mixtures, we relate the global dynamics of the chain to the isoperimetry of the log-scale mixing distribution, and illustrate the effect of heavy-tailed targets by examining inverse-gamma mixing distributions.

papers.title: A bound-preserving hybrid lattice Boltzmann method for scalar hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: Solutions to scalar hyperbolic conservation laws may develop discontinuities within finite time even from smooth initial data, while higher-order lattice Boltzmann (LB) methods tend to generate non-physical oscillations and out-of-bounds behavior near steep gradients. To address this issue, we first construct a first-order LB method with the upwind-type equilibrium distribution functions under the \(DdQ(2d+1)\) lattice structure, and establish its bound-preserving (BP) conditions. We then develop a second-order multiple-relaxation-time LB (MRT-LB) method by introducing the auxiliary source distribution functions, and analyze its \(L^2\) stability. Building on these, we propose a hybrid LB method that preserves the collision-streaming structure, by conservatively mixing first- and second-order updates through a convex constraint mechanism. We further establish the global BP (GBP), local BP (LBP), and relaxed LBP (RLBP) limiters in the hybrid LB method, together with the associated macroscopic BP constraints. Numerical experiments examine the convergence order, interface capturing performance, and discontinuity resolution capability of the proposed BP hybrid LB method. The results indicate that it effectively suppresses out-of-bounds behavior in the second-order LB method and reduces numerical dissipation in the first-order LB method, while maintaining the prescribed bounds and discrete mass conservation.

papers.title: Quantum Sensing of Defects
papers.abstract: Metrology of defects (or impurities) is a major challenge in quantum sensing, with implications for material science, nano-scale metrology, and the development of high-precision quantum devices. In this work, we employ single and multi excitation sensors for the metrology of defects, with the system Hamiltonian encoding the structure of the sensor and the defect treated as a perturbation potential. We evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the ground state of the system to quantify the metrological performance of the sensors in locating a defect and in estimating its coupling strength. In doing so, we identify two distinct sensing regimes, determined by the ratio between the defect screening parameter and the inter-sensor site spacing, and establish the scaling behavior for the resulting estimation precision. Furthermore, we analyze the joint estimation of defect position and strength as well as the performance of two-excitation sensors, demonstrating how the number of excitations and their interactions influence sensitivity. Our results provide tools for optimizing defect detection with quantum sensors, with potential applications in solid-state quantum technologies.

papers.title: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
papers.abstract: A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected. A full correspondence packing is a collection of such colorings that uses every color at each vertex exactly once. We prove a conjecture of Cambie, Cames van Batenburg, Davies, and Kang [Random Structures & Algorithms 64 (2024), 62--93]. For every sufficiently large $D$, there is a positive integer $k(D)=(1+o(1))D/\log D$ such that every correspondence cover of any finite bipartite graph has a full correspondence packing if each color has at most $D$ forbidden partners and each vertex has $k(D)$ colors. More precisely, we prove this conclusion with \[ k(D)=\left\lceil\frac{D}{\log D-2\log\log D-6}\right\rceil \] for every integer $D\ge\lceil e^{20}\rceil$.

papers.title: Quantitative homogenization of $k$-Hessian equations in periodic media
papers.abstract: Let $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the $k$-admissible solutions of $σ_k(D^2u^\varepsilon)=f(x,x/\varepsilon)$ and $σ_k(D^2u)=\overline f(x)$ on a bounded convex domain $Ω$, with the same Dirichlet data. Here, $f$ is uniformly positive and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline f(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}f(x,y)dy$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove $\|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α}$ for all $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $f\in C_x^{m,α}(\overlineΩ;C_y^{2,γ}(\mathbb T^n))$ for some $0<γ<1$. Periodic cell estimates give smooth dependence of the correctors on the background Hessian and the normalized density. The divergence-free property of the Newton tensor cancels the first macroscopic correction and yields the higher rate. Both exponents are optimal in general, already for $n=k=1$.

papers.title: Scale profile, nesting, and the $A_2$ growth of dyadic paraproducts
papers.abstract: For the dyadic paraproduct $π_b$ and $Q\ge1$, let $Φ_b(Q)$ be the supremum of $\|π_b\|_{L^2(w)}$ over dyadic weights with $[w]_{A_2^d}\le Q$. Beznosova's linear bound $Φ_b(Q)\lesssim Q\,\|b\|_{\mathrm{BMO}_d}$ is sharp over $\mathrm{BMO}_d$, while every nonzero symbol safisfies $Φ_b(Q)\gtrsim Q^{1/2}$. We ask which properties of a fixed symbol place its growth between these extremes, and identify two: the distribution of the Haar coefficients of $b$ over scales and the nesting of their supports. Symbols supported on $L$ consecutive scales obey a two-weight bound of order $\sqrt L$; as a consequence, polynomial decay of the scale tails determines the sharp trowth exponent, except at a critical rate where the growth is determined up to a factor $(\log Q)^{1/2}$. For symbols supported on a chain, $\sup_Q Q^{-1/2}Φ_b(Q)$ is comarable to $\|S_d b\|_{\infty}$, and for every symbol the boundedness of the dyadic square function $S_d b$ is necessary for minimal growth $Q^{1/2}$. Conversely, $Φ_b(Q)\lesssim Q^{3/4}\|S_d b\|_{\infty}$ for every symbol, and the bound $\|π_b\|_{L^2(w)}\lesssim [w]_{A_2^d}^{1/2}\|S_d b\|_{i\infty}$ holds for every symbol at weights whose local $A_2$ imbalance has bounded evergy off a family of dyadic chains with disjoint tops; this class contains all weights used in our lower bounds.

papers.title: Non-tempered GGP conjecture for classical groups: the Bessel case
papers.abstract: In their recent paper, Gan, Gross and Prasad proposed a precise conjecture to describe the restrictions of representations of classical groups that lie in an L-packet of Arthur type. On top of local root numbers, the main notion considered is the relevance of two A-parameters. In this paper, we establish that the relevance of two A-parameters is sufficient for the existence of a Bessel period for a pair of representations in the associated L-packets. Moreover, such a pair is unique. We also prove the necessity of relevance for co-tempered A-parameters, and give several counterexamples in the general case.

papers.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
papers.abstract: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

papers.title: Parallelizable Interior-Point ADMM for Block-Structured Nonconvex Programs
papers.abstract: Physics simulation is an increasingly important computational primitive for AI, and local--global/ADMM splitting exposes its parallel structure but lacks matching finite-time convergence guarantees. We close this gap with two ADMM variants, Interior-Point ADMM (IP-ADMM), for block-structured nonconvex composite programs with smooth nonlinear inequality and affine constraints. A one-sided finite-activation wall keeps each constraint split state strictly feasible while the original-space infeasibility vanishes, giving closed-form constraint updates, one proximal call per objective block, and one equality-constrained quadratic consensus solve per iteration. \rev{To our knowledge, this makes IP-ADMM the first single-loop method that updates nonconvex inequality constraints locally and in parallel with finite-time convergence guarantees.} Ordinary IP-ADMM attains a CQ-free best-iterate weak-KKT rate of $O(K^{-1/3})$ or a banded Fritz--John rate of $O(K^{-1/4})$, which converts to KKT at $O(K^{-1/4})$ under a uniform constraint qualification; these are nearby-point certificates that reduce to conventional KKT for smooth blocks. A checkpoint variant, IP-ADMM-Ckpt, improves the asymptotic KKT exponent to $O(K^{-1/3})$. We also show how the bounds scale with the objective- and constraint-block counts and the coupling norm.

papers.title: Tangent lengths and invariants of Poncelet polygons between two circles
papers.abstract: A polygon inscribed in one circle and circumscribed about another moves in a one-parameter family, by Poncelet's porism. We study this family through the tangent lengths from the vertices to the inner circle and find a number of quantities that remain constant during the motion. For example, the sum of the fourth powers of the distances from the circumcenter to the points of contact, plus twice the squared area, is constant. We also obtain a version of Euler's formula for $n$-gons, extend a problem on bicentric hexagons from Kvant, and find a second quadratic invariant that goes along with the classical theorem of Weill. The basic invariants have elementary proofs; for the main ones we give two proofs, one of them without derivatives. Reciprocation at a limiting point of the two circles turns these results into statements about billiards in ellipses, and gives short proofs of theorems of Akopyan, Schwartz and Tabachnikov and of Bialy and Tabachnikov. Using the elliptic curve of the family, we show that the area determines the polygon up to a reflection, find the polygons of largest and smallest area, which proves two conjectures of Cieślak and Mozgawa, and find all points for which the product of the distances to the vertices is constant.

papers.title: Isospectral Density Design and Distinct Global Shape Transitions in Weighted Yukawa Droplets
papers.abstract: We study Euclidean perimeter plus Yukawa repulsion with a fixed radial source density and a fixed ordinary volume. For each sufficiently small positive screening parameter, we construct two smooth, positive, strictly increasing densities whose constrained shape Hessians at the unit ball agree for every coupling. Their source masses, Yukawa moments, and ball self-energies also agree. Just above their common first global transition threshold, all minimizers form one rotation orbit of tetrahedral shapes for one density and one orbit of sectoral threefold shapes for the other. Both transitions are continuous, and the minimizing shapes are strictly convex. We obtain the two densities by fixing the boundary data that determine the Hessian and changing the higher derivatives that determine the reduced quartic energy. We compute a positive quartic coefficient, restore the three scalar observables by interior corrections, and add a finite exterior density barrier to control all finite-perimeter competitors.

papers.title: Quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering in nonlocal plasmonics
papers.abstract: We establish quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering by a fixed collection of smooth, separated metallic particles described by the hard-wall generalized nonlocal optical response (GNOR) model. As the ratio $η$ of the reference screening length to the particle size tends to zero, regularized first-order and second-order transmission conditions approximate the electric far-field operator with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively. The estimates retain retardation and are uniform on compact subplasma frequency intervals with fixed positive damping and for a bounded dimensionless diffusion-to-pressure ratio. The proof combines exact elimination of the longitudinal field, a uniform weak bound for its boundary density, and smoothing by exterior observations. The same error orders hold for fields observed at a fixed positive distance from the particles. We also justify thin-coating representations on bounded tangential wave-number ranges for a planar interface and on fixed finite spherical angular subspaces. For each fixed quasistatic spherical multipole with a simple local pole, the first- and second-order models approximate the pole and its residue with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively.

papers.title: Möbius Invertibility of Rank Invariants
papers.abstract: One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. Möbius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, Möbius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support. This work studies the extent to which Möbius inversion can be extended beyond these finiteness conditions. Namely, we formalize the notion of Möbius invertibility, which captures when Möbius inversion exists beyond these finiteness conditions, and investigate when the GRI is Möbius invertible. A central result we establish is that Möbius invertibility of the GRI is guaranteed for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules when $d\leq 2$, but may fail when $d>2$. Establishing this failure also corrects an error in the existing literature. In response to this higher-dimensional obstruction, we show that for finitely presentable $d$-parameter persistence modules, restricting the GRI to intervals subordinate to the finite grid supporting a minimal free presentation preserves its Möbius inversion whenever the latter exists over all intervals. Since computing the GRI over all intervals in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is infeasible in practice, this result provides a principled justification for restricting the GRI to those intervals.

papers.title: Hyperbolic Polynomial Certificates: Universality, Cubic Exactness, and a Weak--Strong Separation
papers.abstract: We study certificates of polynomial nonnegativity based on hyperbolic polynomials and their parameterized Bézoutians and establish three results. First, in the unrestricted hyperzout model of Ng and Saunderson, every nonnegative real form of degree $2r$ in $m$ variables admits a hyperzout representation using an auxiliary hyperbolic form of degree $2r$ in $m+1$ variables with parameters $k=1$ and $μ=r+1$. Second, every homogeneous hyperbolic cubic in five real variables is SOS-hyperbolic in Saunderson's fixed-direction sense: for each hyperbolicity direction $e$, $B_{p,e,v}$ is a matrix SOS for every $v\in\Lam(p,e)$. Third, a general localization proposition turns an interior-SOS central Wronskian and a non-matrix-SOS central Bézoutian into a two-direction weak--strong separation. An icosahedral seed gives a rational example of degree $46$ in $43$ variables for which every $W_{u,v}$ on the cone is an SOS, but some $B_{p,u,v}$ is not a matrix SOS. The obstruction persists at nearby interior directions, giving a rational hyperbolicity direction at which the polynomial is weakly SOS-hyperbolic but not SOS-hyperbolic in Saunderson's fixed-direction sense. The construction is supported by exact rational Gram and trace certificates.

papers.title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
papers.abstract: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions. In this study, we propose a physics-informed neural network to efficiently calculate the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators. By incorporating three types of loss functions, we train a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to satisfy the governing PDE for the asymptotic phase and the adjoint equation for the phase gradient. The trained network delivers the phase function accurately and, via automatic differentiation, allows the calculation of the phase gradient governing the oscillator's response to perturbations, which enables rapid entrainment closed-loop control using strong inputs. We validate the approach using three types of limit-cycle oscillators and demonstrate that the PINN can facilitate fast and global phase-locking control.

papers.title: Spectral Instability of Wasserstein Entropy on Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: Let $M$ be a compact homogeneous Riemannian manifold, and let $m$ be its invariant probability measure. At $m$, the Wasserstein entropy Hessian has a sharp lower bound given by $λ_1$, the first positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on $M$. We study how this bound changes under perturbations of the density by counting the generalized Hessian eigenvalues below $λ_1$. Using a Schur complement and Peter-Weyl triple products, we reduce this count to the first eigenspace and its interaction with higher modes, including isotropy multiplicities. We apply this method to two important families of homogeneous manifolds. On the unit round sphere $S^d$, $d\geq 2$, we prove that the bound $λ_1=d$ holds only at the uniform density and obtain an exact local index formula for every nonzero smooth mean-zero perturbation $η$. Writing its degree-two component as $x^{\mathsf T}Qx$, the index at $1+\varepsilonη$ is $n_-(\varepsilon Q)+\dim\ker Q$ for sufficiently small nonzero $\varepsilon$. On the normal complete flags $SU(N)/T^{N-1}$, we find a perturbation with complementary indices $N(N-2)^2+2N-1$ and $(N-2)(3N-1)$ under opposite signs, whose proportions tend to one and zero as $N$ grows. A resonant example on $S^1\times S^2$ shows that spherical rigidity does not hold on every homogeneous manifold.

papers.title: Large-time behavior of solutions to the 1D nematic liquid crystal with $γ>1$
papers.abstract: We study the large-time behavior of solutions to the system modeling the compressible flow of nematic liquid crystals with a polytropic equation of state $P(ρ)=ρ^γ$ $(γ>1)$ in Lagrangian coordinates. In contrast to the isothermal case $γ=1$ treated in [4,5], we establish a new representation formula for the specific volume (Lemma 2.2) and, using Jensen's inequality, derive time-uniform estimates that yield global upper and lower bounds for the specific volume. A key ingredient is the reconstruction of the $D$--$Z$ structure for $γ>1$, which gives an exponential decay of $Z(t)$ and thus overcomes the difficulty caused by the power-type pressure.

papers.title: On Lie-Algebraic Conditions for Finite-Dimensional Koopman Bilinear Embeddings of Control-Affine Systems
papers.abstract: Koopman bilinear representations for control-affine systems have attracted considerable attention. In this paper, we investigate, from a Lie-algebraic perspective, conditions under which a control-affine system admits a finite-dimensional Koopman bilinear embedding. Specifically, we focus on the Lie algebra generated by the drift and control vector fields. First, we show that the finite-dimensionality of the generated Lie algebra is a necessary condition for the existence of a Koopman bilinear embedding. Next, when the generated Lie algebra contains a nonzero nilpotent ideal, we derive a sufficient condition for the existence of such an embedding. Finally, through an example of a quadratic polynomial system, we demonstrate that the finite-dimensionality of the generated Lie algebra imposes strong restrictions on the vector fields, suggesting that exact finite-dimensional Koopman bilinear embeddings may be nongeneric.

papers.title: On the Convergence of Continuous-Time AdamW
papers.abstract: Continuous-time AdamW provides a framework for understanding whether an optimizer widely used to train large-scale neural networks settles to an equilibrium or sustains persistent motion. We study this long-time behavior while retaining bias correction and fixed positive weight decay. Under suitable assumptions, we establish that the dynamics are well defined for all time and remain bounded when the decay is sufficiently small. Our main result connects their limiting behavior to the geometry of the objective: trajectories approach a locally invariant manifold whose dimension equals the Hessian nullity along the associated critical component. When critical points are isolated and have at most one such direction, the trajectory converges to a single equilibrium. With two degenerate directions, however, bounded persistent motion can occur even for a smooth, strictly convex objective with a unique minimum. We also quantify how close the long-time trajectory remains to the critical set as weight decay decreases, without assuming convergence to a point. These results identify objective geometry as a key to understanding when continuous-time AdamW converges and when persistent motion is possible.

papers.title: Approximation and Error Bounds for Zero-Sum Stopping Games with Probability Criteria
papers.abstract: This paper studies a two-person zero-sum stochastic game, which must terminate when either player quits the game or a state of the game first enters a prescribed target set. The performance criterion is the probability that the total reward reaches a given threshold. First, under a mild condition, we prove the existence of the value and a Nash equilibrium of the game by developing a comparison theorem. Second, for solving the game with infinite states, we develop a finite-state approximation method based on truncation, and derive explicit error bounds between the values of the truncated and original games. Third, using the error bounds, we design an effective algorithm, by which we can not only obtain any approximation of the value and Nash equilibria of the original game, but also provide convergence analysis of the approximation. Finally, a queueing example is used to illustrate the advantage of our condition and the effectiveness of our algorithm.

papers.title: Efficient scheduling of particle annihilation for long-time Wigner simulations
papers.abstract: Particle annihilation (PA) plays an indispensable role in alleviating the numerical sign problem in long-time simulations with the Wigner branching random walk (WBRW) method. However, the effect of PA frequency on long-time accuracy remains poorly understood, leaving its choice largely empirical. To provide systematic guidance for PA scheduling, we establish an overall error estimate for PA through a uniform mesh, separating WBRW variance, resampling variance and squared bias. The analysis shows that, beyond merely controlling particle growth, PA replaces the exponential-in-time variance bound with a linear-in-time bound, thereby alleviating the numerical sign problem. It also reveals bias-variance trade-off induced by PA frequency: frequent PA limits variance but can increase accumulated bias. More importantly, building on the newfound error structure, we propose a variance-constrained cost optimization strategy for adaptive PA scheduling across several PA methods. An intrinsic-time reparameterization provides a common clock for variance control, PA scheduling, and branching dynamics under time-dependent potentials. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical variance behavior and bias-variance trade-off, and results of our schedule populate the low-cost regime of the empirical Pareto frontier objecting to balance accuracy and efficiency.

papers.title: Quasi-F-split heights and derived Morita invariance
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-F-splitting from the viewpoint of non-commutative algebraic geometry. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. For a proper dg-category over k with a Serre functor, we define quasi-F^e-split heights for e\geq 1 by using finite topological restriction homology with coefficients in a shift of the Serre functor. Using the functoriality of polygonic topological Hochschild homology for laced categories due to Harpaz--Nikolaus--Saunier, we show that these heights are invariant under derived Morita equivalence. For a proper Gorenstein scheme of pure dimension over k, the height for e=1 of its dg-category of perfect complexes coincides with the quasi-F-split height in the sense of Yobuko. For a complete Noetherian Gorenstein local \(k\)-algebra with residue field k, the dg-category of perfect complexes supported at the closed point recovers the n-quasi-F^e-splitting of Tanaka--Witaszek--Yobuko for all n,e\geq 1. The proofs use the computation of the zeroth homotopy groups of TR with coefficients due to Dotto--Krause--Nikolaus--Patchkoria, Zariski descent, and Serre duality or local duality.

papers.title: Khinchin's constant along deterministic subsequences
papers.abstract: Khinchin's theorem says that, for Lebesgue almost every real number, the geometric mean of the partial quotients in its continued fraction expansion converges to a universal constant $K\approx 2.6854520010\ldots$. We show that the same constant is obtained when the partial quotients are sampled along any fixed strictly increasing deterministic sequence of indices. Thus arithmetic progressions, polynomial sequences, prime indices, and lacunary sequences all give the usual Khinchin constant. We also look at a different selection rule: instead of restricting the indices, we restrict the values of the partial quotients. In this case the answer changes. The geometric mean of the prime-valued partial quotients converges almost surely to a new constant $K_{\mathcal P}\approx {3.439477971}\ldots$.

papers.title: Decorrelation Before Variable Selection: Left and Right Transforms and Their Trade-Off
papers.abstract: Decorrelation has two forms. A left transform keeps coefficients and changes noise; a right transform keeps noise and changes coefficients. Cholesky whitening alone keeps noise variables inactive when true ones come first; decorrelation preserving coefficients and noise loses information.

papers.title: An Implementation of the 3-Dimensional Extended Persistent Homology Transform
papers.abstract: The Extended Persistent Homology Transform (XPHT) describes a shape through the extended persistence diagrams of its directional height functions. We present an algorithm for computing a finite directional sample of the three-dimensional XPHT from a triangulated boundary. Our main construction determines essential first-homology pairings by combining an ordered tree-cotree decomposition with evaluation-dual cocycles. The decomposition supplies a homology basis compatible with the height filtration, while the cocycles are used to determine the essential birth-death pairs. Degree-zero persistence and duality determine the remaining boundary diagrams. Under the boundary-reduction hypotheses and with critical-point sign labels, these diagrams yield the extended persistence of the solid. The resulting procedure uses graph constructions and linear algebra over F2 on boundary meshes extracted from three-dimensional binary images.

papers.title: High-dimensional transfer learning with unaligned ordinal responses
papers.abstract: In this work, we study high-dimensional transfer learning with unaligned ordinal responses, allowing different domain-specific regression coefficients, cumulative links and thresholds. We develop the sample-split and full-target algorithms that pool source and target likelihoods and then estimate a target correction. Under suitable conditions, our algorithms achieve minimax-optimal rates for parameter estimation and excess risk. Simulations favor the full-target algorithm over the sample-split algorithm for finite-sample estimation and prediction. An application to a medical dataset further demonstrates the predictive gains of our full-target algorithm over the target-only and pooled baselines when transferring information from the five-category source data to binary hospital mortality.

papers.title: Equilateral-triangle-free sets in finite planes
papers.abstract: For a prime $p>3$, let $F(p)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of $\mathbb F_p^2$ containing no equilateral triangle with nonzero squared side length. Alex Iosevich asked for the exact value of $F(p)$. By constructing such subsets of $\mathbb F_p^2$ from cap sets in $\mathbb F_3^n$, we obtain the uniform lower bounds \[ F(p)\gg \begin{cases} p^{2γ}, & p\equiv 11\pmod{12},\\ p^{1+γ}, & p\equiv 1\pmod{12}. \end{cases} \] Here $γ=\log_3(2.2202)$, so the two exponents are $1.452008666\ldots$ and $1.726004333\ldots$, respectively. We also apply a quantitative corners theorem to show that $F(p)=o(p^2)$ as $p\to\infty$ through either congruence class.

papers.title: The numerical index with respect to a Lipschitz map
papers.abstract: We introduce the Lipschitz numerical range, radius, and index with respect to a norm-one Lipschitz map, unifying the Lipschitz numerical index of a Banach space and the numerical index with respect to an operator. For real-valued maps, we obtain metric formulas on finite metric spaces and graphs. In particular, a connected simple unweighted graph with at least two vertices is bipartite if and only if its real Lipschitz-free space, or equivalently its dual, has classical numerical index one. We also characterize finite metric spaces by universal numerical-radius attainment. Among complete metric spaces, we characterize length spaces by non-denseness of maps attaining their $g$-Lipschitz numerical radius for every norm-one $g$. Moreover, we derive upper bounds for the $g$-Lipschitz numerical index with $\ell_p$ targets, $1<p<\infty$, and lower bounds for the Lipschitz numerical index of spaces with property $β$. Finally, for norm-one operators $G: X \to Y$ between real Banach spaces, we prove $$ n_{G^*}(Y^*,X^*) \leq n_{L,G}(X,Y) \leq n_G(X,Y), $$ with equality in the upper bound whenever $X$ is separable or $Y$ is $1$-complemented in its bidual. This extends recent equality results for the identity operator to arbitrary norm-one operators and a broader class of target spaces.

papers.title: Capacitary Hardy inequalities, Dirichlet boundary conditions, and the limit as $p\downarrow1$
papers.abstract: We use nonlinear Dirichlet resolvents to prove Hardy inequalities with capacity-based and resolvent-based weights for $1<p<\infty$ on arbitrary open sets. On bounded Sobolev extension domains, integrability against either weight characterizes Sobolev functions satisfying homogeneous Dirichlet conditions on arbitrary closed subsets of the boundary. On bounded Lipschitz domains, the resolvent-based weight $\bm{W}_{D,p}$ converges locally in $L^1$ to the negative of Barozzi's interior variational mean curvature as $p\downarrow1$.

papers.title: A singular minimizer of a uniformly convex Hessian-dependent functional
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory à la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

papers.title: Lifting the local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number and $n\ge 1$ an integer. We construct a local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$, following an approach by Shiho. More precisely, consider the ring $W$ of Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic $p$. Let $f:\mathfrak{X}\rightarrow \mathfrak{S}$ be a log smooth morphism of fs logarithmic $p$-adic formal schemes, whose underlying formal schemes are flat and locally of finite type over $W$, and assume the exact relative Frobenius after reduction modulo $p$ admits a lift $F$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be Lorenzon's indexed algebra on the reduction modulo $p^n$ of $\mathfrak{X}.$ We define an indexed subalgebra $\mathcal{B}_F\subset\mathcal{A}$ and equip it with an integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connection. Our main result is an equivalence between the category of indexed $\mathcal{B}_F$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent $p$-connections compatible with the $p$-connection on $\mathcal{B}_F$, and the category of indexed $\mathcal{A}$-modules equipped with integrable quasi-nilpotent connections compatible with the canonical connection on $\mathcal{A}$. This gives a local logarithmic version of the Cartier transform modulo $p^n$.

papers.title: On König's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
papers.abstract: König conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

papers.title: Phase-conjugate Gaussian encoding for continuous-variable quantum key distribution with a single phase-sensitive amplifier
papers.abstract: Phase-conjugate encoding is naturally compatible with shared phase-sensitive amplification and joint detection, offering a compact optical receiver architecture for continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CVQKD). Here, we develop a unified encoding and security framework for two-mode Gaussian CVQKD with tunable phase-conjugate intermode correlations matched to a joint receiver comprising a single phase-sensitive amplifier (PSA) and one balanced photodetector. We present both coherent-state and squeezed-state prepare-and-measure protocols that use the same transmitted ensemble. The two preparations can be implemented through classically precoded Gaussian displacements of coherent sidebands or a directly generated two-mode squeezed vacuum, respectively, without an actual optical mode converter. The encoding and detection scheme separates low-variance joint quadratures for key generation from high-variance joint quadratures carrying private random modulation. This complementary modulation can reduce Eve's Holevo information without changing the Alice--Bob mutual information. Numerical results show that optimized correlated coherent-state encoding achieves higher asymptotic key rates at long distances and extends the positive-key range compared with optimized single-mode coherent-state modulation. The optimal intermode correlation increases with transmission distance, and the range advantage persists under the symmetric correlated two-mode Gaussian attacks considered here. These results provide a theoretical basis for the design and implementation of PSA-enhanced two-mode CVQKD with phase-conjugate encoding.

papers.title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$.
